# poLight and its competitors on the road to top-tier AR/VR/XR glasses — timeline map and commentary

*As of 2026-10-08. Interactive map: `timeline-map.html` (open locally or via the published artifact). Data: `timeline_data.json`. Every dated row carries its source URL; confidence is confirmed (primary source), strong (several reputable outlets), circumstantial (inference) or rumor (forum / unnamed sources).*

## 1. Headline findings

- Meta's developer pages show autofocus is a marketed feature of the VR Glasses passthrough, not how it is delivered. The product page (live 2026-10-08; earliest Wayback capture 2026-09-27, four days after Connect) lists 'Open-periphery color passthrough with autofocus and depth sensing', about 100 g and 'Available Spring 2027'; the compare-devices table (earliest capture 2026-10-05; a 2026-09-08 capture lists only Quest 3 and 3S) says 'Color stereoscopic (26 PPD) passthrough with autofocus and depth sensing'. The US$1,299.99 price comes from Meta's blog of 2026-09-23, which, like the newsroom post, says only 'passthrough camera'; the 300 g puck figure is Road to VR's. GadgetGuy says the colour cameras 'have autofocus' and that eye tracking sharpens what you look at, which does not say how focus is driven; press camera counts conflict. No Meta source names an actuator or supplier.
- The DBS note is now a primary document, but its Meta sentence is still one analyst's unsourced claim. The PDF of 2026-08-26 (the research file puts the passage on page 4; not re-checked) says 'A Meta project combining Q Tech's module capabilities with poLight's low-power tunable-lens technology is expected to enter mass production in 1H27'. It is the first of four DBS Q Tech notes (2025-07-11, 2025-08-12, 2026-03-17, 2026-08-26) to name Meta and the only verified document asserting poLight's lens as a Meta supplier. But it says 'a Meta project', not the VR Glasses, cites no source, and 1H27 is wider than the spring window. On 2026-09-10 poLight's CEO, asked about a Q Tech design-in statement with mass production in H1 2027, said poLight is 'engaged with Q-Tech on several customer projects' and could not comment; that statement was not located, so the two may share a source.
- Q Tech's own TLens record is thin, and its silences are weak evidence. Of 106 English HKEX filings from January 2025 to 2026-10-08 (77 non-routine ones read), the only one whose subject is poLight, per the research file, is the completion notice of 2025-06-05, which calls its actuator 'the best solution for optical module in XR'. The results deck of 2026-08-24 shows 'TLens + AR Mono Engine: Volume Delivery Achieved' and, as a separate bullet, 'Overseas Key Customers: Ramp in 2H26 / 2027', naming no product, customer or unit count. The interim report itemises no poLight transactions, yet poLight invoiced Q Tech NRE of USD 313,141 (March 2026) and USD 178,662 (Q2), so that silence proves nothing. Monthly volumes never name XR, and over 95% of the actuator caps approved on 2026-09-11 are for voice-coil motors, showing only that Q Tech's group can supply VCMs.
- Meta is the only OEM any source pairs with poLight, but that rests on one unsourced sell-side sentence plus an optics relationship that DBS's engine sentence already explains. Q Tech's decks show a 'major US customer' vendor code (2024-03-25), then a 'US M brand' code with projects under discussion (2024-08-12), the letter never expanded; a Kunshan job ad (page marked updated 28 September, year inferred) seeks an XR factory head dealing with brand customers 'such as Meta, Pico'. None of the HKEX filings read names a US customer; DBS's Meta note of 2026-05-08 omits poLight. Asked on 2026-08-19 whether the AR|MR design-in, Q Tech qualification and AR-camera programmes are three different end customers, the CEO said 'Those three are different, but there are more'. Q Tech is 'involved in [...] all these cases, but not alone', and the AR-camera release reuses the 'Top Tier U.S. consumer electronics OEM' wording, so a Q Tech-linked Meta project could be that one, and Apple, Google, Amazon or Snap could be the Q Tech backer.
- No FCC grant identifiable as the VR Glasses or its puck is public as of 2026-10-08, which says nothing about schedule because applications are invisible until a grant issues. Meta certifies under 2AGOZ (itself) and 2AYOA (Luxottica); every identified 2024-2026 grant maps to a launched product, research device or debug tool, except an unmatched charging dock (2AGOZ-M7K, 2024-09-25). Across nine shipped products with original-equipment grants, grant to shipping ran from minus 1 to 68 days, median 35 (six of nine at 33 to 49). With a March-May 2027 sale, the glasses, and possibly a separate puck ID as Pico filed, should be granted about 2027-01-11 to 2027-04-28 (2026-12-23 to 2027-06-01 on the full range; later if launch slips). Meta asks for about 180 days of confidentiality, so internal photos surface around July to October 2027, after launch, and schematics and bills of materials are normally permanently confidential: a grant confirms schedule and radios, not the actuator.
- The trade and shipment sweep could not have found a TLens, so its null result carries no weight. ImportYeti's Meta Platforms Technologies page shows 148 US sea shipments (October 2023 to 2025-06-09) of accessories, packaging and adapters, then a confidentiality marker; its search could not be read, so no poLight page was found. A million lenses at about US$2 each is only some US$2m, below the noise of UN Comtrade and Philippine customs notices. poLight's own reports document the chain: ST-made wafers (none ordered in 2024, 2025 or H1 2026, with inventory said to cover 'several millions' of lenses), Tong Hsing's Philippine assembly (installed capacity about 200,000 lenses a month and test 400,000-500,000 in October 2025, a doubling planned by end-2026) and a Q Tech line still being tuned. The CEO's remark that program units are 'likely coming from the Philippines' is from 2026-02-25, and he added that Q Tech had made only qualification units.
- Oslo Børs filings give no clean insider signal. Executives' dealing since January 2025 is option grants (strike NOK 3.95, 2025-06-16), small offering subscriptions at NOK 2.69 (about NOK 0.19m allocated) and, from 2026-08-14 to 08-26, an exercise-and-sell by the CEO, COO and CTO of 369,862 shares each at an average NOK 12.13 (NOK 13.46m in all), keeping holdings and most options, with no open-market insider buying. The sale used the post-Q2 exercise window and its reason is undisclosed. The largest commitment of the period was Q Tech's own: NOK 171.5m for 63,743,112 shares (29.66% after dilution), locked up to about 2027-06-04 (about 2027-04-15 on its HKEX wording), so its not selling is uninformative. The sweep notes record no flagging notice after Investinor's exit on 2025-11-27 and no net short of 0.5% or more. poLight has issued no exchange notice since the 2026-09-21 TWedge order.
- The LinkedIn trail is unverified. Profiles are login-gated, and round-4 checkers could not open or re-find the pages the researcher read as search snippets: Lidu Huang's Meta record (to April 2025) with a 'miniature piezoelectric tunable lens AF camera module' that passed AR/VR/MR qualification with 'high NTI yields'; a module lead's 'NTI dToF/ Tlens camera module process developments'; and a Hon Hai manager's TLens driver work. Even at face value they are modest: Huang's text names no supplier, he is a named inventor on Meta's own lens filings and left about three months before Program A's first order, so it fits an in-house lens as well as a bought one; the module lead lists nine employers and gives no employer or dates for the bullet; the Hon Hai manager's customers are Amazon, Google and Microsoft. The 'led the autofocus work' post and the 'DRI for TLens' line are forum paraphrases no index returns. No post, profile or ad names poLight, Q Tech, Goertek or Luxshare with Meta.
- Meta's patents point to tunable-lens autofocus work but never to a supplier. Its filings describe window, polymer, glass-membrane and piezo lenses: a lens barrel with an integrated tunable lens (granted 2026-05-19), a wide-FOV assembly (granted 2026-06-23) citing three poLight documents, two of them web pages Meta's side submitted, a piezo driver IC (published 2025-06-05) and an exposed-camera design (published 2026-08-13), beside a gaze-driven autofocus grant (2026-02-10) and a pending non-tunable moving-element MEMS design (priority 2023-12-06). Grants lag filings by two to four years and some families were abandoned, so the filings fit an in-house or co-developed membrane lens as well as a bought TLens-class part. Goertek's four 2024 filings recite 'TLens' or 'T-Lens' in claims, ByteDance's application names 'a poLight lens' among options and Samsung's a 'tunable lens (T-lens)'; Q Tech's, Jiangxi Shengtai's and Goertek's describe poLight's piezo-film-on-polymer construction, while Sunny's and Huaqin's use the term generically. Patents show awareness and options, not purchases.
- Program A has two POs in three announcements: a qualification order of about NOK 1.7-1.8m (2025-08-06, half firm, the rest called 2026-02-11) and a NOK 0.7m follow-on (2026-06-18, deliveries 'likely second half of 2026'), about NOK 2.4-2.5m in all. The announcements span 10.4 months, and 14.1 months after the first order the programme is still described as qualification, with no design-in or production-priced PO. poLight's first-order-to-launch record runs from 2.1 months (Meizu) through 4.8 (Xiaomi watch), 5.9 (XUN) and 7.3 (Honeywell) to about 10 (Magic Leap 2, attribution inferred), with initial mass-production POs of NOK 0.36m and 2.9m; cancelled cases surfaced 9 to 41 months after first orders. If Program A is the VR Glasses camera, a first production-priced PO or design-in could fall between October 2026 and March 2027 on the shorter precedents, but on the 7-10-month ones it would already have fallen between May and October 2026: a distribution, not a due date. A Q3 report still saying 'qualification' is the baseline; the signal is a production-priced PO or design-in, or none by the Q4 report.
- Program B is unidentified, and the earlier lean to Alibaba is lowered by judgement, not by evidence of supply. poLight's four orders (about NOK 4.9m by our sum; about NOK 4.0m for the three of 2026) concern a case it reclassified as a design-in on 2026-07-10, with Q4-2026 deliveries. The CEO calls the customer 'a big company and a major player in the ecosystem', the product 'probably high-end', with a release plan 'this year', still a little uncertain. The sweep's own subjective ranking, not evidence: Pico Space Pro 0.24, Samsung eyewear 0.22, Snap Specs 0.13, Alibaba 0.10, Xiaomi and Xreal Aura 0.07 each, others 0.17 in all. Alibaba keeps the strongest public TLens-glasses link (Ant's reference design pairs a Q Tech 'Tlens' with real-time autofocus, reported 2026-07-22; the CEO: 'we know that initiative. It's Alibaba'). poLight's two MR-headset design-win releases came the day of, and the day after, Varjo launches (2023-11-27; refresh 2025-10-08); Varjo is inferred and both are enterprise cases, so the pattern is weak. Qwen N1's sale on 2026-10-13 is the next dated test; only a teardown settles it.
- Meta's hiring around Connect is actuator-agnostic and concerns the next generation, and its camera glasses carry no autofocus claim. Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 (2026-09-23) keeps its 12 MP camera with no autofocus claim and an unstated focus type, while the VR Glasses announced the same day are listed with autofocus passthrough. A Reality Labs paper of 2025-04-17 counts an autofocus actuator's size, weight and power against always-on glasses, notes autofocus is needed for 1 arcmin over 40 cm to infinity and recommends 2 arcmin fixed focus 'given current technology': a research study, not a product decision. The Camera Architect role (posted 2026-08-19 per a mirror, about 2026-10-03 per LinkedIn) covers 'AF/OIS actuator systems' and a 'focus strategy (fixed-focus vs. AF)' choice; a Strategic Sourcing Manager (LinkedIn datePosted 2026-09-24) will 'onboard new module integrators and key optical component suppliers'. Neither names tunable, piezo or TLens.
- No merchant competitor's XR camera win appears in the dataset, but several products target the market and component suppliers seldom announce wins. CML's last XR-specific article is dated 2024-11-26; a PCT published 2026-04-30 and an October-2026 job ad still cite glasses and AR/VR, and a LinkedIn headline suggests its CTO now works at Apple (dates inferred). Optotune's 0.3 g EL-3.1-10.8 (datasheet 2026-09-18) is 'designed for high-volume OEM integration' and draws 20 mW for a 10 dpt range against poLight's own '<6 mW including driver', figures not stated on the same basis. Varioptic stays industrial; Sheba (17 staff and USD 400K sales on a January-2026 CES listing) has shown no customer since 2024-01-09. The alternatives the data cannot rule out are Meta's own membrane lens, its pending moving-element MEMS design, a TLens-class part from another source and a voice-coil motor, which Q Tech's controlling-shareholder group could supply only if Q Tech is the module maker; Goertek's filing calls VCM focus of about 1 s too slow for gaze-driven see-through video.
- The checkpoints differ in what they can show. poLight's Q3 report (2026-10-29, 07:00) and Capital Markets Day (2026-10-30, Oslo; agenda and speakers unpublished) can move the odds only through company wording: 'qualification' is the baseline for Program A, a design-in or production-priced PO would be news, and product revenue excluding NRE (Q2: NOK 9.1m, with NOK 3.7m recorded as NRE) is an all-customer figure. Qwen N1's in-stock sale on 2026-10-13 tests Program B, not Meta. FCC grants for the VR Glasses and puck are estimated for about January to April 2027 and the Q4 report is scheduled for 2027-02-24; teardowns plausibly follow within days to several months of on-sale (estimated April to September 2027), and only one identifying a poLight PZT-MEMS lens, ideally in a Q Tech module, settles the supplier. For scale, illustration only: if the VR Glasses used TLens (unconfirmed) with two autofocus cameras at the CEO's 'around $2+', 500,000 units would be about US$2m, while the OEM's stated need is 'much higher' than the Q Tech line.

## 2. How to read the map

- **Lanes**: the upper group is the glasses and headset producers, the lower group is poLight and every competing autofocus / tunable-lens supplier plus two evidence lanes (Meta patents & people; analysts, brokers & press).
- **Markers** are dated signals, coloured by category (product, commercial, IP & people, analyst/press). Hollow markers are circumstantial or rumour. A thin line under a marker shows the date's imprecision (month, quarter, half, year).
- **Bars** are launch windows or dated ranges; everything right of the today line is expected, not observed.
- **Washes** on supplier lanes show where supplier milestones are expected for a given future launch, working backwards with optics-industry lead times (see §4).
- **Match lines** connect a supplier signal to the launch it plausibly feeds; click a marker to read why, and what would contradict it.
- **Cadence strips** in the commentary show the days between a lane's updates.

## 4. Where supplier timelines meet future launches

### 4.1 Expected supplier milestone windows (lead-time logic)

**Meta VR Glasses retail launch — US$1,299.99, 25 countries, autofocus passthrough ("Spring 2027")** (2027-03-01 → 2027-05-31), drawn on lanes: poLight (TLens), Q Technology, Camera-module & assembly chain, VCM / SMA actuator makers, Optotune, Cambridge Mechatronics
- design-in / qualification complete: 2025-09-01 → 2026-12-31
- qualification orders expected: 2025-08-01 → 2026-10-31
- production POs / ramp expected: 2026-10-01 → 2027-03-31
- FCC grant(s) for glasses and puck expected (public check): 2027-01-11 → 2027-04-28
- FCC internal photos public (180-day confidentiality): 2027-07-10 → 2027-10-25
- Rationale: Meta VR Glasses, US$1,299.99, 'Spring 2027' (Mar-May 2027): the only announced consumer device due in 2026-2027 with documented 'passthrough with autofocus and depth sensing' (Meta developer pages, earliest captures 2026-09-27 and 2026-10-05); no source names the actuator. Supplier bands use poLight's own record and apply only if Program A is this device: first-order-to-launch ran about 2.1 months (Meizu), 4.8 (Xiaomi watch), 5.9 (XUN), 7.3 (Honeywell design-in PO) and about 10 (Magic Leap 2, attribution inferred), with initial MP POs of NOK 0.36m and 2.9m. Program A's qualification POs (2025-08-06; 2026-06-18) sit 18.8 and 8.4 months out, so a first production-priced PO or design-in could fall between October 2026 and March 2027 on the 2-5 month precedents, while the 7-10 month precedents point to May-October 2026, when only a qualification follow-on appeared: a distribution, not a due date, and cancelled cases surfaced 9-41 months after first orders. Nothing in the band has appeared by 2026-10-08. Regulatory phases: no FCC record identifiable as the glasses or puck exists under 2AGOZ (applications are invisible until grant). Across nine shipped Meta products grant-to-shipping ran -1 to 68 days (median 35; six of nine at 33-49), so a March-May 2027 sale puts the grant(s) at about 2027-01-11 to 2027-04-28 (2026-12-23 to 2027-06-01 on the full range), possibly two IDs as for Pico's headset and puck. Meta's roughly 180-day confidentiality (179-181 days in ten cases) puts first internal photos at about July-October 2027; schematics and BOM are normally permanently confidential, so filings may never name the actuator. Producer-side timing: Phoenix panels in mass production since May 2026 (The Elec), Q Tech's 'Ramp in 2H26/2027' (2026-08-24) and DBS's 1H27 sentence (2026-08-26); poLight ordered no MEMS wafers in 2024, 2025 or H1 2026, so a ramp would show first in product revenue. Phoenix supplier lists name no camera-module or actuator vendor; Meta also holds its own piezo-membrane lens IP and a pending moving-element MEMS autofocus, and VCM and Optotune's liquid lens remain alternatives. First teardowns are expected April-September 2027 (estimate).

**"Artemis" consumer AR glasses (Orion successor) — 2027 per Bloomberg/Reuters; Bosworth non-committal** (2027-01-01 → 2027-12-31), drawn on lanes: poLight (TLens), Q Technology, Cambridge Mechatronics, Optotune, Camera-module & assembly chain, VCM / SMA actuator makers
- design-in / qualification complete: 2025-07-01 → 2026-12-31
- qualification orders expected: 2025-10-01 → 2027-03-31
- production POs / ramp expected: 2026-07-01 → 2027-09-30
- Rationale: Meta 'Artemis' consumer AR glasses, a full-year 2027 rumour window (Bloomberg/Reuters) that Bosworth 'would not commit to' on 2026-09-24, so the bands are wide (12-18 / 9-15 / 3-6-month norms). poLight's consumer-display precedent is a warning: the 2022-03-15 AR display design-in was 'some years' from release in Feb 2024 and a consumer LBS design-in was removed in Aug 2025 with 'no plan for MP'. Program C, the NOK 5m AR-camera design PO of 2025-10-13 with validation modules shipped end-Q2 2026, falls 14.6 and 6.1 months before 2027-01-01, but the CEO said on 2026-08-19 that Programs A, B and C are different customers, so C can be Meta only if Meta is not the Q Tech backer. Meta's 'camera module with tunable lens' (priority 2024-12-19, filed 2025-11-14, published 2026-06-25) allows 'polymer tunable lens technology or liquid lens technologies' with wafer-level optics, replacing the earlier LC/electrowetting reading, and its exposed-camera filing (priority 2025-02-12) describes a piezo-membrane option for AR glasses. Meta's Sep-2026 sensor and 'auto-focus electrical design' postings are design-phase hires 3-15 months before any 2027 device. No supplier is named.

**Quest 4 "Griffin" gaming headset — no earlier than H2 2027, possibly 2028** (2027-07-01 → 2028-12-31), drawn on lanes: Q Technology, Camera-module & assembly chain, VCM / SMA actuator makers, poLight (TLens)
- design-in / qualification complete: 2026-01-01 → 2027-12-31
- qualification orders expected: 2026-04-01 → 2028-03-31
- production POs / ramp expected: 2027-01-01 → 2028-09-30
- Rationale: Quest 4 'Griffin' gaming headset, no earlier than H2 2027 and possibly 2028 (rumor; Bosworth confirmed two devices on the roadmap on 2026-02-10). Quest 3 and 3S shipped 2x4 MP passthrough with no autofocus; if the VR Glasses' autofocus passthrough carries over, design-in would run Jan 2026-Dec 2027 under the 12-18-month norm, and under poLight's own cadence (first orders 4.8-10 months before launch) qualification POs for a 2028 device would surface during 2027. Q Tech's product map lists a 'VR VST TLens AF camera' (2025-08-11), its 2026-09-28 posting for an XR whole-device factory head names 'Meta, Pico' as brand customers, Goertek is the core/exclusive VR ODM for Meta, Sony and Pico with ~80% of high-end assembly (2023-11-18) and Luxshare is building a 9m-unit/yr Vietnam VR line tied to Meta. No direct evidence links any actuator supplier to Griffin.

**Meta Ray-Ban Display successor "Hypernova 2" (binocular) — timing unresolved H2 2026→2027** (2026-07-01 → 2027-12-31), drawn on lanes: poLight (TLens), Q Technology, Camera-module & assembly chain
- design-in / qualification complete: 2025-01-01 → 2026-12-31
- qualification orders expected: 2025-04-01 → 2027-03-31
- production POs / ramp expected: 2026-01-01 → 2027-09-30
- Rationale: Binocular Ray-Ban Display successor 'Hypernova 2', timing unresolved between H2 2026 (The Information, 2026-02-19) and 2027 (Bloomberg, 2025-04-01); not shown at Connect 2026 and Bosworth said on 2026-09-24 there is 'no new version of the hardware', although Citi told clients the same week that a 'Ray-Ban Display 2' is expected early 2027 with Sunny, Konica Minolta and OmniVision positioned (see). Bands follow the same 12-18 / 9-15 / 3-6-month norms. The current Display uses an OmniVision LCoS engine and a 12 MP Sony-sensor camera that TechInsights (2026-06-10) describes without any actuator or autofocus, drawing 1.0-1.7 W; poLight's TWedge wobulation part is not expected to be mass-production ready before about 2028, so a 2027 Hypernova 2 would precede it. Evidence is thin on both display and camera actuators.

## 5. Commentary per lane — what each timeline indicates

### Meta (producer; 115 dated signals)

Meta Platforms / Reality Labs: Quest headsets, Ray-Ban/Oakley/Meta-brand AI glasses with EssilorLuxottica, Meta Ray-Ban Display and the Orion AR prototype. Every camera glasses shipped to date is fixed-focus; the spring-2027 Meta VR Glasses (ex-Phoenix) are the first Meta consumer device whose passthrough cameras are documented as autofocus, making Meta the single most important potential top-tier customer for a tunable-lens or VCM autofocus supplier. Meta Connect 2026 (2026-09-23/24) announced Meta VR Glasses for a spring-2027 launch, the central product for the poLight question; see the Meta file. Included here only as calendar intersections. Meta appears only indirectly: poLight's Q3 2025 deck credits Ray-Ban Meta (>2M units in 2024) as the consumer driver, and the user's brief places a Meta autofocus-camera 'VR Glasses' launch in spring 2027. No poLight document names Meta. Meta as producer: display-side Butterscotch varifocal prototype (2023) and the 2026-09-23 announcement of VR glasses for spring 2027, which falls days after Meta's lens-barrel patent publication and Optotune's glasses-class lens launch. Meta's glasses lineup (Ray-Ban Meta Gen 1/2, Oakley HSTN/Vanguard, Ray-Ban Display, Meta Glasses) all carry 12 MP fixed-focus cameras per teardowns; capacity constraints and doubling plans in early 2026. The Meta VR Glasses announced for spring 2027 are the product window that Q Tech's 2H26/2027 ramp and DBS's 1H27 claim would fit. Meta as a producer: the research brief posits 'VR glasses' with autofocus cameras in spring 2027. The 2022-07 / 2023-02 patent priority dates imply a 3.5–4.5-year priority-to-product lag, consistent with reliability qualification during 2024 and production readiness by April 2025. Product verification is outside this file's scope. Meta announced its ~100 g Meta VR Glasses at Connect 2026 (23 Sept 2026) for spring 2027 at USD 1,299.99, with developer specs confirming color stereoscopic 26-PPD passthrough 'with autofocus and depth sensing' but naming no actuator or supplier. Also the dominant AI-glasses OEM (Ray-Ban Display, ~94% share H1 2026).

Cadence: 88 day/month-dated non-press signals; median gap 8 days overall, 7 days since 2025; longest silence 364 days.

**2019-09-17 → 2023-10-17: Fixed-focus glasses, camera headsets**  
Luxottica co-development began 2019-09-17; Quest 2 shipped 2020-10-13 without colour passthrough; Ray-Ban Stories (2021-09-09) were torn down as fixed focus with 'no voice coil or magnets'. Quest Pro (2022-10-25) and Quest 3 (teased 2023-06-01, shipped 2023-10-10, 131 days, 2x4 MP passthrough) added colour passthrough without autofocus, and Ray-Ban Meta shipped 20 days after its 2023-09-27 announcement. The pattern: glasses ship within weeks of announcement, headsets within months.

**2021-09-10 → 2027-10-31: Regulatory filing cadence and the FCC window**  
Meta certifies through two grantee codes, 2AGOZ (itself) and 2AYOA (Luxottica). Across nine shipped products with original-equipment grants, grant-to-shipping ran from minus 1 day (Ray-Ban Stories) to 68 days (Quest 3), median 35, six of nine at 33-49. Every identified 2024-2026 grant maps to a product, research device or debug tool except the 2AGOZ-M7K charging dock. Nothing identifiable as the VR Glasses or puck is public as of 2026-10-08, but applications are invisible until grant, so that says nothing about schedule. A grant is expected about 2027-01-11 to 04-28, possibly two IDs; photos stay confidential about 180 days, schematics and BOM normally permanently, and an optically tethered glasses unit may need no grant of its own.

**2024-08-29 → 2026-09-13: Roadmap churn and the Phoenix build**  
'Puffin' was first reported on 2024-08-29 for 2027, pulled in to end-2026 (2025-06-02), delayed to H1 2027 (Business Insider memo 2025-12-05, CTEE 2025-12-07) and confirmed by Bosworth on 2026-02-10 alongside Quest 4 'Griffin' (no earlier than H2 2027). Orion was shown 2024-09-25 with commercial AR 'expected 2027'; Aria Gen 2 research glasses (2025-06-04) are fixed-focus global-shutter cameras; the EssilorLuxottica long-term deal (2024-09-17) and ~3% stake (2025-07-09) underpinned 2m Ray-Ban Meta by Feb 2025 and 7m AI glasses in 2025. Meta Ray-Ban Display shipped 13 days after its 2025-09-17 reveal (~84k units in 2025) with a Sony 12 MP camera and no actuator identified (TechInsights 2026-06-10); Gen 2 was confirmed 'simple fixed focus' on 2025-12-11. Phoenix firmware leaks began 2026-02-25; Seeya started mass production of its 0.91-inch OLEDoS panel in May 2026 with >1m shipped by late August after BOE failed qualification; UDN's 2026-09-13 renders show a 'miniature stereo camera array' and a launch 'pushed to 1H 2027'.

**2026-05-21 → 2026-10-13: Program B screen: Meta Glasses and Gen 3**  
Meta's other 2026 glasses do not fit poLight's Program B. The own-brand Meta Glasses (FCC 2AGOZ-G4Q granted 2026-05-21, launched 2026-06-23) carry a 12 MP camera and launched before the 2026-07-10 design-in. Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 (2026-09-23, US$449) keeps the 12 MP camera with no autofocus claim and an unstated focus type; Gen 2 reviews found simple fixed focus. The sweep gives 'a second Meta product' 0.04: poLight treats Program A as a separate customer, and the VR Glasses arrive in spring 2027, not in a 'release plan this year'. This shows only that Meta made no autofocus claim for any 2026 glasses launch.

**2026-06-23 → 2027-09-30: Connect 2026 and the autofocus line**  
Primary copies replace the screenshots, but they establish a marketing claim, not a mechanism. Meta's developer product page (live 2026-10-08; first Wayback capture 2026-09-27, four days after Connect) says 'Open-periphery color passthrough with autofocus and depth sensing'; its compare-devices table (first capture 2026-10-05; a 2026-09-08 capture lists only Quest 3 and 3S) says 'Color stereoscopic (26 PPD) passthrough with autofocus and depth sensing'. Meta's consumer blog and newsroom post of 2026-09-23 say only 'passthrough camera' and omit autofocus and megapixels. Press camera counts conflict. No Meta source or hands-on names the actuator or links poLight, TLens or Q Tech.

### Apple (producer; 31 dated signals)

Apple ships only Vision Pro (2024-02-02; M5 refresh 2025-10-22) and has no glasses yet. Gurman/Kuo put the display-less N50 glasses (two cameras: capture + computer vision) at a WWDC June 2027 unveil, Q2 2027 mass production and late-2027 shipment, after slipping from end-2026. Apple is the most-cited alternative to Meta as poLight's "Top Tier U.S. Consumer Electronics OEM", but no camera-module or focus-actuator vendor is public and the camera configuration was still undecided in July 2026. Apple WWDC 2026 (week of June 8) is listed only as a calendar intersection; see the Apple file. Apple Vision Pro (12 cameras, no module supplier identified in teardown) and the rumored N50 smart glasses with two cameras, originally slated for Dec-2026 mass production/early-2027 launch and later pushed to late 2027 per Bloomberg. No supplier or autofocus detail reported. Apple's tunable-lens filings (2018, 2023, 2024; inventors including ex-CML CTO Richard Topliss) are for fluid-filled see-through prescription lenses in head-mounted devices, not camera autofocus. No Apple glasses-camera AF tunable-lens filing surfaced; Apple camera architect Patrick Llull moved to Meta in May 2026. Strongest alternative identity for poLight's unnamed top-tier U.S. OEM if not Meta; Vision Pro sold ~390k in 2024 and first lighter smart glasses are reported for late 2027. Q Tech's lack of Apple exposure argues against Apple being the Q Tech-backed customer.

Cadence: 16 day/month-dated non-press signals; median gap 46 days overall, 98 days since 2025; longest silence 1685 days.

**2018-09-21 → 2025-10-22: Vision Pro cycle, no actuator evidence**  
Apple's tunable-lens patents (2018-09-21, 2023-05-03, 2023-07-21 with ex-CML CTO Topliss, 2024-03-12 with SMA) are all see-through prescription lenses, not camera autofocus. Vision Pro shipped 242 days after its 2023-06-05 announcement with 12 cameras and no actuator or module supplier identified; the M5 refresh shipped 7 days after announcement (2025-10-22) while production fell to 45,000 units in Q4 2025 from ~390,000 in 2024. The display-accessory glasses were paused Q4 2024 and cancelled January 2025.

**2024-01-01 → 2026-10-06: Register sweep: no Apple TLens trace**  
The round-3 full-text sweep for 'TLens' and 'poLight' across all assignees returned no Apple text that survived the register check: a lens-power metrology grant (US 12,523,846, 2026-01-13) whose variable-focus camera uses liquid-filled or liquid-crystal lenses was left off the map as off-topic, a head-mounted lens-mounting grant matched only on 'lens tabs', and two further Apple list hits were not opened. Apple's tunable-lens patents already on the map (2018-09-21, 2023-05-03, 2023-07-21 with ex-CML CTO Topliss, 2024-03-12 with SMA actuators) remain fluid-filled see-through prescription optics. Across 2024-2026 publications there is no Apple text on a piezo-membrane camera autofocus, no poLight citation and no N50-related camera filing. The absence fits Gurman's two-sensor design with no autofocus reported, but a buyer need not patent a part, and the 18-month publication lag hides anything filed after about April 2025.

**2025-05-23 → 2027-12-31: N50 slippage**  
Gurman's targets moved from end-2026 (2025-05-23, with 'large quantities of prototypes' at end-2025) to reveal-2026/ship-2027 (2025-12-12), mass production December 2026 and launch early 2027 (2026-02-18), late 2027 (2026-05-31) and a WWDC June 2027 unveil with shipments by end-2027 (2026-07-26, reiterated 2026-09-27): about 12 months of slip over 492 days. The design has two camera sensors, capture and computer vision, with no autofocus reported; Kuo expects Q2 2027 mass production and 3-5m+ units in 2027, display glasses in 2029 and the N224 headset on 'life support'. Supplier-side evidence is thin: ex-CML CTO Ben Brown's move and SEMCO's coil deal point to Apple's existing actuator chain, not poLight. Round 2 added only chain-level pointers: Cowell, Vision Pro's external-camera supplier with Apple at 98.1% of revenue, 'hopes to join the Apple AI-glasses project' (Guojin, 2025-11-03); Patrick Llull left Apple for Meta in May 2026 and ex-Apple optics inventors lead Meta's tunable-lens camera-module filing; a forum-posted profile of an Apple Grenoble hardware engineer with PZT tunable-lens research background is rumor-grade.

### Google / Android XR (producer; 15 dated signals)

Google owns the Android XR platform (announced 2024-12-12) and co-designs the first glasses, but Samsung builds the hardware (SM-O200P/J) and Xreal builds Aura. Roadmap: audio/camera AI glasses fall/November 2026, display glasses 2027, Gucci/Kering 2027. Google is a U.S. OEM in name, but camera-module sourcing for the 2026 glasses runs through Samsung's supply chain; no AF/actuator disclosure found. Google I/O 2026 (May 19–20) carried Android XR glasses updates; Google also bought part of HTC's XR team ($250M, Jan 2025) and partners with Magic Leap and Samsung. Included here only as calendar/cross-link intersections; see the Google file. Google / Android XR is an alternative OEM or ecosystem candidate (possibly for poLight's platform-style NOK 5m AR camera project), with 2026 audio and display glasses built with Samsung, Warby Parker and Gentle Monster.

Cadence: 14 day/month-dated non-press signals; median gap 64 days overall, 42 days since 2025; longest silence 154 days.

**2024-05-01 → 2025-12-08: Platform assembly**  
The Magic Leap partnership (May 2024, extended three years on 2025-10-30), Qualcomm's confirmation of joint glasses work (2024-09-05), Android XR's unveiling (2024-12-12), the US$250m HTC acqui-hire (2025-01-23) and Google I/O 2025 prototypes with Gentle Monster, Warby Parker (US$150m commitment) and Kering set the stage; Galaxy XR launched 2025-10-21 and Google said on 2025-12-08 'the first glasses will arrive next year'.

**2026-04-16 → 2027-12-31: 2026 launch, 2027 display**  
Kering's CEO put Gucci glasses at 'probably next year, 2027' (2026-04-16); I/O 2026 (2026-05-19) committed Samsung/Google eyewear to 'this fall', display glasses to 2027 and Xreal Aura to before end-2026; Unpacked London (2026-07-22) formally introduced the eyewear and the FCC cleared SM-O200P/SM-O200J on 2026-10-01 with a Samsung official naming November 2026, 689 days after the Android XR unveil and 166 days after I/O. Nothing from Google addresses camera focus; the 2027 display generation is the window where any new camera module would be designed in.

### Samsung (producer; 28 dated signals)

Samsung is the hardware lead of the Android XR alliance: Galaxy XR shipped 2025-10-31 (US$1,799.99) and display-less intelligent eyewear (Snapdragon AR1 Gen 1, single 12MP camera) was introduced 2026-07-22 and FCC-cleared for a November 2026 launch; a micro-LED display model ("Haean") is expected 2027. Any focus actuator in these glasses would most plausibly come from Samsung's smartphone (SEMCO-centred) VCM chain; nothing ties poLight, CML, Optotune, Alps or Q Tech to Samsung glasses, and Samsung is not a U.S. OEM. Samsung introduced Android XR 'intelligent eyewear' (AR1 Gen1, Gentle Monster / Warby Parker frames) at Unpacked London 2026-07-22 with availability 'this fall'; the Feb 2026 Unpacked showed no glasses. Details are in the Samsung/Google file; included here only as calendar intersections.

Cadence: 17 day/month-dated non-press signals; median gap 41 days overall, 38 days since 2025; longest silence 773 days.

**2021-07-15 → 2027-12-31: Samsung's T-lens depth-camera family**  
Samsung's register trail is two families, neither naming poLight. US 12,487,379 (priority 2021-07-15, granted 2025-12-02) claims a 7-element lens with a tunable lens between the second and third elements, a polymer plate over sealed liquid-gel pressed by a ring whose actuator 'may include a piezoelectric actuator or a motor'; a Meta application cites it. KR priority 2022-10-31 and its US continuation 19/182,755 (filed 2025-04-18, published 2025-07-31, docketed, no office action) describe a glasses-type device whose second camera's 'focus-variable lens 280 may be a tunable lens (T-lens)' of piezo film, glass membrane, glass panel and transparent polymer, for depth-from-focus. Cadence: priorities in 2021 and 2022, then a US continuation 30 months later, six months before Galaxy XR and 19 months before SM-O200P. The T-lens serves a depth camera that the single-camera FCC device lacks, so it neither confirms nor contradicts the VRARA autofocus rumour; a 2027 examination outcome is a projection.

**2023-01-01 → 2025-10-31: Headset first**  
Joint OS/silicon/hardware design with Google and Qualcomm began in 2023; Project Moohan was named 2024-12-12 and shipped as Galaxy XR on 2025-10-31, ten days after its unveil, at US$1,799.99 with 2x6.5 MP passthrough plus 10 tracking cameras; an aggregator estimates ~40,000 units in 2025. No autofocus was claimed for the passthrough cameras.

**2025-03-21 → 2026-11-30: Glasses: a 19-month slip and an autofocus rumour**  
ETNews reported 'Haean' glasses for 'later this year' on 2025-03-21; three weeks later the target became 2026, repeated at the Q4-2025 call, MWC (2026-03-06), I/O (2026-05-19, 'this fall') and Unpacked (2026-07-22). A Samsung official then named a November 2026 launch (reported 2026-10-01), about 590 days after the first report (to 2026-11-01). The FCC grants of 2026-09-27 (A3LSMO200P and J) have public exhibits, a SAR report and label among them, that mention no camera; the single 12 MP camera comes from press. Autofocus is claimed only by GalaxyClub (2026-01-13) and VRARA's 'early reports' (2026-02-09, 230 days before the FCC grants); Samsung has not confirmed it, and the leaked spec sheet names a Sony IMX681 at US$379-499.

**2026-01-13 → 2027-03-26: Program B candidate: intelligent eyewear**  
Samsung's eyewear ranks second in the sweep's subjective ordering as a Program B candidate (0.22). For: the design-in of 2026-07-10 came 12 days before Unpacked, a November launch, a camera suited to QR payment, and the only autofocus claim on any 2026 glasses, GalaxyClub's 'met autofocus'. Against: the Maeil/Wellsenn text it cites does not mention autofocus in English; XRVision's 2026-02-04 'very likely liquid lens' rests on that one word; the product is Korean-led, display-less and mass-market against the CEO's 'U.S. and China'; SAR testing began 2026-02-26, more than four months before the design-in; and Program B's POs equal roughly 150-190k lenses against a 2024 rumour of 500,000 first-run units. Samsung's pages say only 'a built-in camera'; photos and manual go public on 2027-03-26 and may show the module.

Snap has shipped camera glasses since 2016 and AR-display Spectacles since 2021; its first consumer AR product, Specs (US$2,195, 51° FOV, 2 RGB + 2 IR cameras), opened pre-orders 2026-09-16 with shipping 'later this fall' 2026 in the US, UK and France. Spectacles shipped in 2016 (vending machines), 2018 (220,000 pairs cumulative by May 2018), 2019, 2021 (first AR display, developer-only) and 2024-09-17 (gen 5, 2 RGB + 2 IR cameras, 226 g, US$99/month for developers). Specs rank third as a Program B candidate (0.13): US, true AR, US$2,195, shipping 'later this fall' in the US, UK and France with no ship date, which fits poLight's silence, and Snap said on 2026-09-16 the computing is built into the glasses 'without a puck or tether'. Against: 'a big company' and 'leading consumer OEM' fit loosely, nothing links Snap to Q Tech or any TLens supplier, and the FCC mirror shows no grant under Snap's code 2AIRN (latest 2AIRN-005, 2024-10-21) or any Specs Inc code although shipping is promised this season. The first run is reportedly capped near 100,000 units, while Program B's POs, about NOK 4.0m, imply roughly 150-190k lenses at about US$2. Snap committed to a 2026 launch at AWE on 2025-06-10 and unveiled Specs 371 days later, still without a ship date.
