### poLight (TLens) (supplier; 277 dated signals)

poLight's qualification customer is a "Top Tier U.S. Consumer Electronics OEM"; the 2025-10-13 PO was explicitly for the design of a TLens camera for AR applications, and a follow-on order puts deliveries likely in H2 2026. Among Apple, Google and Samsung, only Apple and Google are U.S. companies, and neither has any public autofocus or actuator disclosure for their glasses; the H2 2026 delivery window lines up better with Meta than with Apple's Q2-2027 mass production. poLight's disclosed AR design wins are Vuzix Shield (industrial, dual TLens autofocus cameras, April 2024) and SnkeXR (medical, Oct 2025), plus an unnamed consumer-electronics AR/MR device with a NOK 2.4m follow-on order (April 2026) and a 'first consumer AR/MR design-in' disclosed in August 2026 for a 2026 launch. None of the six OEMs in this file has a public link to poLight. Only historical design-in evidence in this scope: Yole records Xiaomi's Mitu 4Pro (Jan 2020) as the first commercial TLens product. No link from poLight to any of the glasses OEMs covered here was found. poLight ASA (Oslo Børs: PLT) sells the TLens piezo-MEMS tunable lens, already inside enterprise AR/MR cameras (Magic Leap 2, Vuzix Shield, SnkeXR). Three separate consumer AR|MR programs are public: Program A (Q Tech-backed top-tier U.S. OEM qualification, POs Aug 2025/Feb 2026/Jun 2026), Program B (leading consumer OEM, reclassified as first consumer design-in on 2026-07-10 with launch expected 2026) and Program C (NOK 5m AR camera design for a top-tier U.S. OEM). poLight never names Meta and has never stated 2027. poLight reference points found in this file: invited SPIE AR/VR/MR talks in 2025 and 2026 (where CML was absent), the Q Tech partnership backed by a 'US top-tier customer' and TLens's '<6 mW' power claim used as the benchmark against CML SMA. poLight (fabless, Norway) makes the TLens PZT-piezo tunable lens; ST fabs the actuator wafers and Asian partners assemble. AR2025 reports no new MEMS wafers ordered in 2025, 55% of deliveries to AR/MR, and three POs tied to a Top-Tier U.S. consumer OEM AR program; a fresh ST wafer order would be a leading indicator of a volume ramp. poLight ASA (Oslo), maker of the TLens piezo-MEMS autofocus lens fabbed at ST's Agrate fab. Its releases track qualification orders from the Q Tech-linked top-tier US OEM (Aug 2025, Oct 2025, Feb 2026, Jun 2026), a separate first consumer AR/MR design-in (Aug 2026), and the progress of the Q Tech TLens line; the only teardown-confirmed XR win is Magic Leap 2. poLight's own IP (2006 → 2025, including the Phair and Tallaron patents cited by Meta), its SPIE invited talks in Jan 2025 and Jan 2026, and the Oct 2025 – Sep 2026 order stream from an unnamed top-tier US consumer OEM for TLens cameras in AR head-worn devices, including a qualification-program PO and a mass-price strategic TLens PO. Recent filings (lead-free TLens, low-power driver) point at consumer-qualification requirements. Norwegian supplier of the TLens piezo-MEMS tunable-lens autofocus (TLens Silver, Add-In, PD50 driver) and TWedge. Runs three separate consumer programs: the Q Tech-backed top-tier U.S. OEM qualification (A), the Oct-2025 ~NOK 5m AR head-worn camera project (B) and the 2026 consumer AR/MR design-in (C). poLight has never named Meta.

Cadence: 250 day/month-dated non-press signals; median gap 6 days overall, 2 days since 2025; longest silence 1668 days.

**2005-01-01 → 2018-12-31: IP, foundry and IPO**  
Founded in Horten in 2005, with the core TLens patent priorities from 2006-09-21 (expiring from September 2026) and the Meta-cited filings of 2014-07-18 and 2017-06-30. ST became the thin-film piezo partner in 2014-09 with 'volume production H2 2015', after an SVTC deal in 2011 that already targeted ~1M units/month; the 2017 plan was 400 to 1,000 wafers/month. Funding ran ahead of revenue: NOK 145m pre-IPO (2015-02-03), NOK 160m at a NOK 610m post-money (2016-08-15) and the IPO of 2018-09-27 (NOK 130m at NOK 50, market cap NOK 401m) with TLens 'ready for introduction in the smartphone camera module market'; first trading day 2018-10-01.

**2019-08-15 → 2021-12-31: First launches: the lead-time record**  
The wearable PVT PO of 2019-08-15 (33,320 lenses, 'not a design-win') and the launch-prep POs of 2019-10-11/17 led to the Xiaomi Mitu watch on 2020-01-07, 4.8 months after the first order and named by poLight only in the Q1-2020 report; XUN Max Pro followed 5.9 months after its PO (2020-02-10) and 125k lenses shipped in 2019. Honeywell's EX30 went from design-in PO (2020-03-05, NOK 0.5m) to release (2020-10-14) in 7.3 months with a validation PO three months out; MAXHUB's webcam took 5.4 months PoC-to-launch (2021-04-06). The other side of the record began at once: the smartphone project was cancelled for 'portfolio' reasons (2021-07-29), Xenocor's NOK 4.0m mass-production-preparation POs (Aug-Sep 2021) never shipped, and the '19 AR projects' deck of 2021-10-29 promised three design-wins within 1H 2022 and 1.5M/month capacity by mid-2022. The first AR design-win (Magic Leap 2, NOK 360k) came 2021-12-01; placements of NOK 40m (2020-04) and NOK 125m at NOK 110 (2021-09-13) funded it.

**2022-01-01 → 2024-12-31: Enterprise XR wins, consumer stalls**  
Magic Leap 2 reached GA on 2022-09-30, 10.0 months after the design-win, with follow-on MP POs 1.5 months before GA (NOK 1.2m) and in Nov 2023 (NOK 0.35m); Yole's teardown confirmed the lens on 2023-03-02. Meizu's design-win PO (2023-01-24, NOK 2.9m) was followed by announcement in 2.1 months and sale in about 4.5; LLVision's Leion Pro went design-in to MP in 1.2 months (2023-04-04); the MR HMD design-win was declared the day Varjo announced XR-4 (2023-11-27); Vuzix Shield's TLens win was confirmed on 2024-04-08 after the 'mid-2023' release slipped about ten months; XVisio never converted. The consumer AR display design-in of 2022-03-15 (PO >NOK 3.5m, follow-on NOK 2.9m on 2023-12-19) was 'some years' from release by Feb 2024 and removed in Aug 2025 with 'no plan for MP', 41 months later. Rights issues of NOK 135m at NOK 10.45 (2023) and NOK 140m at NOK 2.3085 (2024, TERP -30%) carried the company; the pipeline sat at 4 design-wins, 3-4 design-ins and 11-14 PoCs through 2024, the first paid TWedge kits were ordered in Q2 2024, and FY2024 revenue was NOK 9.6m with TLens in 28 products.

**2024-01-09 → 2025-02-03: Filing cadence 2024-2025: cost, power, thermal**  
The sweep's full-text read of poLight's own filings shows a new priority every two to three months from mid-2024: a lead-free tunable lens and an optical assembly citing two Meta filings (2024-07-16), a ring-actuated lens with a 3-30 mm membrane (2024-10-29), hexagonal lenses to maximise wafer packing (2024-12-20) and a low-power hold-mode driver (Danish filing, 2025-02-03) whose text names 'TLens Silver Premium' as its test load. Grants ran in parallel: US 11,870,371 (2024-01-09), US 12,066,619 (2024-08-20), US 12,164,101 (2024-12-10). The subject matter is mostly cost per wafer, power, drivers and reliability, plus one larger form factor, consistent with preparing volume. Nothing names a customer, XR device or product; apart from the driver text the descriptions never use the TLens trade name, describing 'a deformable, non-fluid lens body' between a bendable membrane and a back substrate. Priorities after about April 2025 would still be unpublished, so the apparent stop after February 2025 is not evidence of a stop.

**2025-01-01 → 2027-12-31: Publications, grants and 2027 national phases**  
Publications arrived roughly monthly through 2026: the tunable-astigmatism family (January 2025, listing 'a pair of AR-VR glass/spectacles' among uses), wobulation calibration (2025-10-30), an optical assembly citing Meta prior art (2026-01-22), ghost/flare mitigation (2026-03-05), passive thermal compensation (2026-03-25), the hexagonal lens (2026-06-25), wobulation video (2026-08-05) and the driver PCT (filed 2026-02-02, published 2026-08-06), found by the round-3 check after an earlier 'PCT not found' verdict. Grants: US 12,405,406 (2025-09-02), US 12,493,178 (2025-12-09) and the 2021-priority thermal-expansion family (EP 2026-03-11, US 2026-05-12). National-phase entries for the 2024-10-29 and 2024-12-20 priorities fall due between late April and late July 2027, a dated checkpoint on which markets poLight pays to protect. The trail is mostly manufacturing and maintenance (thermal, flare, packing, drivers, TWedge) and says nothing about who buys the lens; with the 2006 core priorities expiring from September 2026, the moat shifts to these filings.

**2025-04-15 → 2026-06-18: Q Tech alliance and Program A**  
Q Tech bought 32.97% at NOK 2.69 (NOK 171.5m) on 2025-04-15, a deal management said one long-standing top-tier U.S. OEM 'triggered' after qualifying TLens 'for many years'. Program A's first qualification PO (~NOK 1.7-1.8m, 50% firm) came 2025-08-06, its final 50% was called on 2026-02-11 and a second PO of NOK 0.7m followed on 2026-06-18 with deliveries 'likely second half of 2026' and 'still several milestones to pass'; on 2026-02-25 the CEO called it a 'mature PoC' that becomes a design-in only when the OEM locks the design and completes component qualification, with qualification units partly made at Q Tech and programme units 'likely coming from the Philippines'. Program C, a NOK 5m PO of 2025-10-13 to design a TLens camera for AR head-worn devices, shipped validation modules at end-Q2 2026. Cash rose from NOK 135.8m (Q1 2025) to NOK 298.2m (Q3 2025); no new MEMS wafers were ordered in 2025 or H1 2026 because inventory covers several million lenses, written down for age only.

**2025-06-16 → 2026-10-08: Insiders, holders, shorts and the 2026-09-10 answers**  
Insider dealing is sparse and not clean. Executives took option grants at a NOK 3.95 strike (2025-06-16) and small offering subscriptions at NOK 2.69, then nothing until 2026-08-14, when the CEO, COO and CTO each exercised 369,862 options and sold the shares at an average NOK 12.13 (NOK 13.46m in all), keeping existing shares and most options. The sale used the routine post-Q2 exercise window and its reason is undisclosed: weak evidence either way. The largest commitment was Q Tech's own NOK 171.5m placement; its 63,743,112 shares (29.66%) are locked up to about 2027-06-04 (about 2027-04-15 on its HKEX wording). The sweep notes record no flagging notice after Investinor's exit (2025-11-27) and no net short of 0.5% or more (not dated rows). On 2026-09-10 the CEO said poLight is engaged with Q Tech on several customer projects and cannot comment on the Q Tech reference.

**2025-11-24 → 2026-07-10: Program B from PoC to design-in**  
A 'leading consumer OEM' placed POs of NOK 0.9m (2025-11-24, a 'mature proof-of-concept' order), 2.4m (2026-04-07), 0.8m (2026-05-20) and 0.8m (2026-07-10), NOK 4.9m in 228 days and one project per the CEO; on the fourth PO poLight declared its first consumer AR|MR design-in, with 'release plan is this year' and Q4-2026 deliveries. The three 2026 POs (NOK 4.0m) are at mass-production price (~US$2+ per lens) for 'a big company and a major player in the ecosystem' (2026-08-19). The CEO declined to locate it; 'U.S. and China, so you pick' described poLight's AR/MR focus. Only Alibaba's Qwen N1 was unveiled after the design-in (previewed 2026-09-10, 62 days later, close to Meizu's 2.1 months); Pico Space Pro, Samsung/Google eyewear, Snap Specs and Xreal Aura were shown earlier and fit only a Q4-2026 sale. AR|MR reached 86% of Q2-2026 revenue and H1-2026 revenue (NOK 20.6m) exceeded FY2025 (NOK 20.5m).

**2026-07-10 → 2026-12-31: Program B: candidates and the Varjo rule**  
No source names Program B (our label). Ninety days after the 2026-07-10 reclassification as a design-in, poLight has issued no design-win release; its last exchange notice was the TWedge PO of 2026-09-21. The CEO's clues: 'a big company and a major player in the ecosystem', 'U.S. and China, so you pick', 'probably high-end' and a release plan 'this year', 'a little bit uncertain'. The three 2026 POs total about NOK 4.0m by our sum, roughly 150-190k lenses at about US$2. poLight's two MR-headset design-win releases came on the day of Varjo's XR-4 launch (2023-11-27) and the day after its refresh of 2025-10-08; Varjo is inferred, both are enterprise cases and earlier AR wins ran months ahead of launch, so the 0-1 day rule is weak. The sweep's subjective ranking (Pico Space Pro 0.24, Samsung eyewear 0.22, Snap Specs 0.13, Alibaba 0.10, Xiaomi and Xreal 0.07 each) identifies no customer.

**2026-08-06 → 2027-02-24: Watch window**  
On the Q2 call (2026-08-06) the CEO called Q Tech-line lenses 'tested and qualified', said a ramp 'depends on the OEM backing that investment' and that major OEMs hold near-zero inventory and avoid 'super high volumes' at first; on 2026-08-19 he said Programs A, B and C are 'different' customers ('but there are more'), that labels are 'confusing you by design', that the design-in OEM is already engaged on other cases and that two lines and a new final-test machine double capacity by end-2026. The CEO, COO and CTO sold 1,109,586 shares at an average NOK 12.13 after an option exercise (reported 2026-08-27); a ninth TWedge sample PO (NOK 1.2m, still TS5) came 2026-09-21; Luxshare showed a 'T-LENS Camera' at CIOE (2026-09-10/11); and poLight filed nothing from 2026-09-22 to 2026-10-06, across Meta's announcement, the longest gap since the Q2 report. The stock closed near NOK 14.90 on 2026-09-25. Dated checkpoints: the Q3 report (2026-10-29), the Capital Markets Day with an external market review (2026-10-30) and the Q4 report (2027-02-24, five days before the VR Glasses window). Only if Program A is the VR Glasses camera do poLight's precedents put a first, probably small, production PO in October 2026 to early 2027.

**2026-10-06 → 2026-10-30: CMD run-up and the Q3 test**  
poLight filed no exchange notice between 2026-09-22 and 2026-10-08, a 17-day gap since the TWedge PO. Its LinkedIn feed shows the company at the VISION 2026 machine-vision fair (about 6-8 October) with industrial messaging and no AR mention, and a Capital Markets Day post of about 7 October promising 'demos, guest speakers, and Q&A' with the agenda pending. The CMD (Friday 2026-10-30, 09:00-15:00, Pareto Securities, Oslo) follows the Q3 report (2026-10-29, 07:00) and promises an 'external review of key strategic markets'. Hard tests: the Program A wording ('qualification' is the baseline; a design-in or production-priced PO is news), product revenue excluding NRE (an all-customer figure), MEMS wafers ordered (informative only above existing inventory) and Q Tech line status. Nothing shows any Program A or B disclosure planned.

### Q Technology (supplier; 84 dated signals)

Q Technology, poLight's strategic investor and module partner. The only Meta link in this file is a Xueqiu forum post asserting Q Tech supplies Quest tracking/passthrough modules and that its TLens tie-up positions it for Meta glasses; no HKEX/IR primary source exists. Q Technology (HK:1478) bought 32.97% of poLight in April 2025 'with backing from a top tier U.S. consumer electronics customer' and built a dedicated TLens assembly/test line (equipment installed Oct 2025, lenses qualified by Aug 2026, NRE invoiced USD 313k + 179k). Its FY2025 deck places TLens and TWedge on a 2026 XR roadmap, making it the module-level bridge between poLight and the unnamed OEM. Q Technology is simultaneously poLight's largest shareholder and TLens production partner, and (via its controlling shareholder) the new owner of TDK's camera-module actuator business with 2,000+ patents and SMA routes. Its FY2025 deck puts TLens on the 2026 roadmap and targets Top-2 actuator rank, so a Q Tech-built XR camera module could use either technology. Q Technology invested NOK 171.5 M in poLight on 2025-04-15 'backed by a top tier U.S. consumer electronics customer' and is building a dedicated TLens assembly/test line in China; poLight invoiced USD 313,141 of NRE in March 2026 for qualifying it for mass production, with work continuing through 2026. Q Technology (1478.HK), Kunshan camera-module maker and poLight's largest shareholder (~30%), building a dedicated TLens assembly-and-test line and, via its controlling shareholder, absorbing TDK's actuator unit (Actutek). Its semi-annual decks give the only dated primary-source ladder from "US M brand vendor code" (Aug 2024) to "TLens volume delivery achieved" and "Overseas Key Customers ramp 2H26/2027" (Aug 2026), but no filing names Meta. Q Technology, poLight's manufacturing partner: Chris Liu (GM Q Tech IoT BU since Oct 2021) and Louis So sit on poLight's board, and the Q3-2025 deck reports a TLens assembly and final-test line at Q Tech under process qualification, with initial lens yield 'not so bad' by Q1 2026. Relevant as the capacity leg of any top-tier OEM design-in. Camera-module maker and poLight's largest shareholder (~NOK 171m, ~one-third stake since June 2025), backed by a top-tier U.S. customer; building a dedicated TLens assembly/test line. Holds a 'US M brand' XR vendor code since 2024 and absorbed TDK's actuator business, so it could supply Meta with VCM or TLens modules.

Cadence: 80 day/month-dated non-press signals; median gap 7 days overall, 7 days since 2025; longest silence 648 days.

**2020-03-31 → 2027-12-31: Q Tech's own TLens filings**  
Q Tech's register trail predates and then tracks the poLight alliance. CN111277742B (priority 2020-03-31, granted 2024-07-19) mentions a 'T-lens camera' only in its background; utility model CN220798387U (filed 2023-07-25, granted 2024-04-16) claims a 'T-lens device' between sensor and lens with a glass-support/polymer/glass-film/piezo-film stack, about 21 months before the 2025 stake. Then two filings 25 days apart during line qualification: CN122171171A (filed 2026-03-30, published 2026-06-09) derives diopter from polymer warpage 'taking tunable lens TLens as an example', so every device can be measured 'throughout mass production', claim 10 reciting the stack; CN122690782A (filed 2026-04-24, published 2026-09-04) pairs a generically named 'Tlens' with metalenses in a TOF module. Both published 2.3-4.4 months after filing and are in examination; the register check classes both as general camera. Neither names a customer or device, and no patent matches the 'VR VST TLens AF camera' on the 2025 product map.

**2021-10-01 → 2025-04-28: Vendor code to alliance**  
Chris Liu took over the IoT business unit in October 2021. The FY2023 deck (2024-03-25) reported a 'vendor code of major US customer'; 140 days later the H1-2024 deck named it 'US M brand' with a design-win target 'within this year'. The FY2024 deck (2025-03-18) said Q Tech was 'qualified as the supplier for multiple international leading manufacturers' of VR/AR/AI glasses, echoed by 开源证券 (2025-03-10) and 国盛证券 (2025-03-19); 28 days later it invested NOK 171.5m in poLight 'backed by a top tier U.S. consumer electronics customer', which 潮电智库 read within 15 days as 'very likely Meta' (2025-04-30), and 13 days after that signed the framework to buy TDK's camera-actuator business, including SMA routes and a Philippines plant.

**2025-01-09 → 2026-09-17: HKEX volumes and the poLight holding**  
HKEX filings run on a fixed beat: 20 monthly volume releases on the 8th-12th with no gap (January 2025 to August 2026), interim results in late August and annual results in mid-March. None names XR, glasses or TLens. IoT is only 1.1-2.4m modules a month, so a ramp of hundreds of thousands of TLens cameras would not show. August 2026 moved to Mobile, Automotive and IoT categories; September's release is due 9-12 October. The poLight holding appears only as equity-accounted lines: 29.90% at 2026-06-30, carrying value RMB 94.75m (RMB 105.98m in December against a fair value of RMB 292.7m), share of loss RMB 11.37m, no June fair value test and no poLight related-party line, although poLight reports invoicing Q Tech NRE. Its one dedicated filing is the completion notice of 2025-06-05; the 2025-04-15 signing has none.

**2025-04-28 → 2026-09-23: Connected transactions: Actutek and the VCM caps**  
The actuator business sits in Mr He's private group, not the listed company. After TDK's framework (2025-04-28) came the Actutek carve-out, closing on 2026-06-01, thirteen months after the framework, and the connected-transaction announcement of 2026-07-27. The new framework replaces the Heyuan Youhua agreement with caps of RMB 325m (September-December 2026), 765m (2027) and 870m (2028); the EGM passed it on 2026-09-11 with the He group abstaining. Over 95% of the caps cover the voice-coil 'Major Product' range (which includes OIS and variable-aperture motors); first-half 2026 purchases were RMB 285.8m (Heyuan Youhua 188.4m, TDK/Actutek 97.4m), and the circular puts new-supplier qualification at two to six months. No piezo, SMA, TLens or poLight wording appears. Executive director Fan Fuqiang, on poLight's board since 2026-08-13, bought 218,000 shares on 2026-09-23 (HKD 1.13m, holding 0.25%).

**2025-06-09 → 2026-03-31: Line build, qualification and roadmap**  
The HKEX note of 2025-06-09 called poLight's piezo actuator 'the best solution for XR optical modules'. The H1-2025 deck (2025-08-11) put 'VR VST TLens AF camera' and 'AR SWIS TLens AF camera' on the product map with a '2026: Light Engine, TLens, TWedge, AR DSA' roadmap. By Q3 2025 the dedicated TLens line had 'all equipment installed' and was producing for trials (poLight call, 2025-10-30); the 河源友华 VCM procurement agreement was renewed for 2025-2027 (2025-11-10). In February-March 2026 the CEO said Q Tech was involved in all three top-tier programmes 'but not alone', that Q Tech-made units were going through temperature, humidity and drop qualification against Philippines units, and that the line was 'limited by only having one test machine' which 'that U.S. OEM' would need to fund; poLight invoiced USD 313,141 of 2025 NRE in March 2026. The FY2025 results (2026-03-16: revenue RMB 20.88bn, profit +435%) reported 'small-batch deliveries for 2 leading overseas terminal clients', 10 brands, a 2026-2030 plan to be top-2 in XR opto-mechanical modules, and the TDK closing 'well underway'.

**2026-04-24 → 2026-09-28: Volume wording and the Meta name**  
On 2026-08-06 poLight's CEO called Q Tech-line lenses 'good and qualified', with some process tuning, and said the ramp depends on the OEM's investment; on 2026-08-19 he called a second line 'a doubling' but not built for 'that OEM'. The 2026-08-24 deck lists 'TLens + AR Mono Engine: Volume Delivery Achieved', 'Deliveries to 2 Top Overseas OEMs' and, as separate bullets, 'Overseas Key Customers: Ramp in 2H26 / 2027' (Chinese: 'expected'). DBS (2026-08-26) writes that a Meta project with Q Tech modules and poLight's tunable lens should reach mass production in 1H27: sell-side inference. A 2026-09-28 Kunshan XR-factory posting names 'such as Meta, Pico' as example clients. On 2026-09-10 poLight's CEO would not map an investor's quote of a Q Tech H1-2027 design-in statement, never located, to any poLight design-in. Q Tech's stake in poLight is 29.66% after dilution (2026-08-25).

### Cambridge Mechatronics (supplier; 58 dated signals)

Cambridge Mechatronics (UK) designs SMA wire actuators, controller ICs and firmware, licensed to Alps Alpine, GalaxyCore, TDK and others, shipping in 100M+ smartphones. It is the most credible mechanical alternative to poLight's TLens for autofocus in glasses, with a five-year trail of anonymous 'commercial engagements' with US tech giants in AR/VR, a 2026 deformable-lens patent for glasses/headsets and a job ad citing 'AI glasses' — but no named XR customer, order or production disclosure. Cambridge Mechatronics: SMA actuator maker with 'commercial engagements with US technology giants' since Oct 2021, SPIE XR talks in 2022–2023, a $40m raise in 2024, and 2024-priority filings (WO2025186538/9, WO2026087900) for SMA-deformed liquid/gel lenses in AR/VR headsets. Meta's SMA-flavoured two-stage-actuator application citing CML was allowed then abandoned in May 2025. Ex-CML CTOs Topliss and Brown now appear at Apple. Cambridge Mechatronics, the strongest competitor candidate: SMA AF+OIS actuators in mass production via licensees (Alps Alpine), Zero Hold Power, and a 2026 deformable-liquid-lens application. Its patents appear in Meta filings and it cites 'US technology giant' engagements, but its licensing model leaves no public order trail; SMA versus piezo is the key technical distinction.

Cadence: 56 day/month-dated non-press signals; median gap 32 days overall, 32 days since 2025; longest silence 6985 days.

**1995-06-21 → 2021-08-06: Smartphone-scale SMA**  
Incorporated 1995-06-21; first SMA OIS design wins with Hutchinson and Foxconn shipped in September 2014; a TDK manufacturing licence followed in 2017 (TDK had bought Hutchinson for US$126m in 2015). 2021 brought ultra-slim OIS+AF (2021-04-21), first driver ICs (2021-07-02) and a Tokyo office. Everything shipped was smartphone volume, tens of millions of units.

**2021-10-18 → 2024-02-13: XR push**  
The San Francisco office opening (2021-10-18) claimed 'multiple commercial engagements with the US technology giants... AR/VR devices'; SPIE AR/VR/MR talks followed on 2022-01-20, 2023-01-25 ('already engaged in commercial projects with several industry leaders') and 2024-01-29, with a CES 2023 showcase of zero-hold-power focus for displays and cameras. Patents climbed from 500 (2021-12-22) to 700 (2024-02-09) and the US$40m round closed 2024-02-13 with Intel Capital and Sony. Meta's 2022-05-31 wearable-camera filing cited four CML documents, the only producer trace of these engagements.

**2024-03-04 → 2026-10-06: Pivot and silence**  
Two XR patent priorities (2024-03-04 and 2024-10-24) describe SMA-driven deformable or liquid lenses 'for glasses and... VR/AR headsets' (published 2025-09-12 and 2026-04-30), but CML was absent from SPIE 2025 and 2026 and its last XR-facing article is dated 2025-05-12, 512 days ago. A new CEO arrived 2025-04-10, Meta abandoned its CML-citing application on 2025-05-08, and CTO Ben Brown's tenure ended in March 2026 with his headline now 'Apple'. Share allotments on 2024-06-26, 2024-09-26, 2026-04-08 and 2026-06-01 suggest rolling equity raises; the live 'AI Vision Product Manager' ad cites 'AI glasses' and ~850 patents, so the ambition persists without a named XR customer.

### Optotune (supplier; 23 dated signals)

Optotune's EL-3.1-10.8 electromagnetically-actuated liquid lens appears only as a reference row from the brief (20 mW @10 dpt, 1.72 mm thick, ms response, datasheet listing AR/VR); not re-verified here. Optotune (Dietikon, CH) makes voice-coil-actuated shape-changing liquid lenses and is the only tunable-lens rival with a glasses-class part: EL-3.1-10.8 (1.72 mm, 0.3 g, 3.1 mm CA, 20 mW @10 dpt), launched 2026-09-21 but documented for OEMs since 2025-09-17. No XR design win, financing or XR talk found; its AR page promises custom lenses to volume production. Optotune's liquid-lens filings target smart-glasses and AR/VR optics (ring-actuated lens 2023, gravity-coma compensation 2024). Its US20160202455A1 was cited by the EP search report against Meta's lens-barrel family. No Optotune camera-AF presence at SPIE AR/VR/MR 2025–2026. Swiss tunable-lens maker whose EL-3.1-10.8 electromagnetic liquid lens (1.7 mm, 0.3 g, 20-85 mW) launched Sept 2026 targeting AR/VR OEM integration. The clearest identifiable direct technological alternative to TLens, though with higher power consumption.

Cadence: 13 day/month-dated non-press signals; median gap 113 days overall, 90 days since 2025; longest silence 1265 days.

**2008-01-01 → 2023-03-14: Industrial liquid-lens leader**  
ETH spin-off founded 2008; Slovakia plant 2017; 100 employees 2018; one-millionth component 2021. The December 2022 brochure listed 250 employees, >300k units/yr cleanroom capacity and AR/VR as a market, while the EL-3-10 datasheet (revisions 2020-12-01 and 2023-03-14) remained a 3 mm industrial part. Stanford's 2017 focus-tunable VR display work used Optotune lenses, the lane's only XR research trace.

**2023-08-30 → 2026-09-21: A glasses-class part surfaces**  
Eyewear-specific patents were filed 2023-08-30 (non-circular ring-actuated lens) and 2024-06-24 (gravity-coma compensation for smart glasses). The EL-3.1-10.8 handling instructions carry a 2025-09-17 date, a US Sales Manager for 'industrial and consumer applications' was posted 2026-01-08, and the datasheet (2026-09-18: 1.72 mm high, 0.3 g, 3.1 mm aperture, 20 mW at 10 dpt, 1 ms response) preceded the LinkedIn launch on 2026-09-21, 369 days after the handling document and two days before Connect 2026. Headcount is now 180+ (from 250) with 2+ million units shipped; no customer is named and the CCM page lists phones, action cams and robotics.

### Corning Varioptic (supplier; 10 dated signals)

Corning Varioptic (Lyon) sells electrowetting liquid lenses positioned explicitly 'for industrial applications'; packaged parts are ≥3.5 mm thick. Corning's AR role is high-index waveguide glass, not autofocus, and its 2026-27 event calendar is entirely machine vision. Corning Varioptic electrowetting liquid lenses offer barrel-free autofocus but are positioned for industrial, scientific and medical vision rather than consumer AR; no public Meta link was found. poLight names Corning among its tunable-optics competitors.

Cadence: 6 day/month-dated non-press signals; median gap 958 days overall, 1010 days since 2025; longest silence 2166 days.

**2007-01-01 → 2019-06-30: Pioneer, then Corning**  
Liquid autofocus lenses deployed since 2007 and a smartphone OIS+AF lens (B617, 2011-01-24, 'up to 90% less power' than VCM) never reached phone volume; Parrot sold Varioptic to Invenios (2016-12-29) and Corning absorbed it in 2017, nearly doubling capacity in 2018 and delivering the 2-millionth lens by June 2019, all to machine vision, barcode and medical.

**2022-01-28 → 2027-05-31: Industrial only**  
Corning's XR presence is high-index waveguide glass (2022-01-28, 2023-12-19) with no liquid-lens mention; the Varioptic page of 2026-09-24 reads 'adjustable lens solutions for industrial applications' and the Oct 2026-May 2027 show calendar (VISION Stuttgart, ITE, Photonics West, Vision China, Automate) contains no consumer or XR event. Meta's lens-barrel examiner cited Varioptic as prior art only. Seven-plus years without a consumer signal.

### Sheba Microsystems (supplier; 9 dated signals)

Sheba Microsystems (Toronto) offers MEMS sensor-shift autofocus (<10 mW, <5 ms) and launched an AR/VR/XR headset camera on 2024-01-09, but had 17 staff and USD 400K sales in 2026 with no disclosed customers. A June-2026 COO hire signals an industrialization push. Sheba Microsystems offers MEMS sensor-shift autofocus for compact AR/VR cameras; its June 2026 Teledyne MEMS partnership concerns ADAS cameras, not glasses. Judged low-probability for the Meta socket given limited consumer-volume maturity.

Cadence: 8 day/month-dated non-press signals; median gap 121 days overall, 154 days since 2025; longest silence 453 days.

**2015-01-01 → 2024-10-10: Launches without customers**  
Founded 2015 (or 2016), Sheba launched an athermalising MEMS AF actuator on 2023-09-21, a sensor-shift AF camera 'for AR/VR/XR headsets' (<10 mW, <5 ms) on 2024-01-09, and the Sharp-7 automotive AF camera on 2024-05-16 with a DXOMARK report on 2024-10-10; no XR customer has been named in any release.

**2026-01-06 → 2026-06-25: Scale check**  
The CES 2026 Ontario delegation listed 17 staff and USD 400K annual sales (2026-01-06); a COO was appointed 2026-06-09 and Teledyne named as MEMS production partner for ADAS actuators on 2026-06-25. 1,001 days after the XR camera launch the company remains an automotive-leaning start-up, not a candidate for a 2027 top-tier programme.

### VCM / SMA actuator makers (supplier; 20 dated signals)

Samsung Electro-Mechanics (SEMCO) designs and makes camera lenses and actuators in-house and in December 2025 was reported close to its first FP-coil (AF/OIS actuator component) supply to an unnamed "global big tech" whose profile matches Apple, with "potential expansion to XR devices". This is the only actuator-supply signal found around the three OEMs and points to conventional VCM, not tunable lenses. VCM is poLight's named primary competitor ('very tough competition from VCM'). Q Tech's controlling shareholder is acquiring TDK's micro-actuator (VCM) assets, so Q Tech can offer both VCM and TLens camera modules to the same OEM. Conventional VCM/SMA actuator makers: Alps Alpine (CML-licensed SMA mass production since Jan 2023, piezo zoom), MinebeaMitsumi (AF VCM since 2005), TDK's camera-actuator unit (carved out as Actutek, incl. SMA 'memory metal' IP, sold to Q Tech's controlling shareholder) and Korean OIS suppliers. No public evidence of any supplying autofocus actuators for XR glasses. VCM/SMA actuator makers; here the TDK camera-module actuator business (Micro Actuator Solutions) carved into Actutek and acquired by Q Tech's controlling shareholder between April 2025 and June 2026. Shows the Q Tech group now offers VCM/OIS alternatives alongside TLens, so a Q Tech module does not by itself imply TLens. Incumbent conventional actuator makers (MinebeaMitsumi VCM since 2005, Alps Alpine VCM and CML-licensed SMA, TDK's actuator business now in the Q Tech group). Meta patents also describe VCM solutions, so a conventional actuator remains a ~10% alternative in the thread's estimates.

Cadence: 17 day/month-dated non-press signals; median gap 77 days overall, 48 days since 2025; longest silence 2548 days.

**2005-01-01 → 2023-01-24: Incumbents**  
MinebeaMitsumi has built VCM/OIS actuators in Cebu since 2005 and Alps Alpine's bi-directional AF actuator entered mass production 2016-01-19; TDK bought Hutchinson (CML's SMA partner) in 2015-11. Alps started SMA actuator mass production on 2023-01-10 (30 um wire, ~40% smaller than VCM) and sampled a piezo zoom actuator on 2023-01-24, showing the incumbents already own alternatives to piezo membranes.

**2024-12-03 → 2026-09-11: Actutek Philippines: actuators, not TLens**  
The Philippine plant that Q Tech's controlling shareholder bought from TDK is a different site from poLight's lens line. TDK opened a second Laguna factory on 2024-12-03 (PHP 2.5bn, 400-plus hires, products not stated); Actutek Philippines Corporation was registered with the SEC in July 2025 and appears as consignee on a Bureau of Customs notice dated 2026-02-09. TDK Taiwan's notice of 2025-11-14 expected the sale by the end of March 2026; completion came on 2026-06-01, about two months late. Philippine job listings put its products at voice-coil holders and optical-image-stabilisation actuators, and Q Tech's decks label it 'Actuator'; nothing shows camera-module assembly, TLens handling or XR work there. First-half 2026 purchases from TDK/Actutek were RMB 97.4m beside Heyuan Youhua's 188.4m. The actuator chain running through Q Tech is VCM-type in every document on file.

**2025-04-28 → 2026-09-26: Consolidation into Q Tech's orbit**  
TDK's framework to sell its camera-actuator business to Q Tech's controlling shareholder (2025-04-28) led to the Actutek carve-out (2025-11-14), effective 2026-01-15, and a completed transfer on 2026-06-01 to the controlling-shareholder group, a connected person of the listed company rather than Q Tech itself; Everbright counted 2,000+ patents and 2,000+ employees and called micro actuators 'decisive' for AF and zoom. Q Tech's connected-transaction caps for actuators and related products run RMB 325m (Sep-Dec 2026, EGM passed 2026-09-11), 765m (2027) and 870m (2028), covering motors, connectors, brackets, housings and tooling, so VCM and SMA volumes will flow through Q Tech whatever happens to TLens and poLight's main module partner can offer either. LG Innotek held over 50% of iPhone 17 folded-zoom OIS (2025-10-01), and SEMCO was negotiating a first fine-pitch-coil supply to an unnamed 'global big tech' with 'potential expansion to XR devices' (2025-12-17). On the Meta side, a closed Seoul posting gave 'AF camera actuator (e.g. VCM)' as a preferred skill and the moving-element AF application cites LG Innotek, Samsung and Nidec art; Alps showed no XR actuator at CES 2026; Mitsumi appears among Meta's VCM patent references (2026-09-26). No row covers Samsung's own camera-actuator sourcing.

### Camera-module & assembly chain (supplier; 85 dated signals)

Camera-module and assembly chain around Meta: Goertek (Quest, Ray-Ban Meta, Display engine, reportedly Phoenix), Luxshare (Vietnam VR line), Sunny Optical (camera modules), EssilorLuxottica assembly. Analyst and press supply-chain maps place the fixed-focus AI-glasses cameras with Sunny; no source yet names the autofocus camera module or actuator vendor for the 2027 VR Glasses. Camera-module and assembly chain evidence for these OEMs: LG Innotek was reported as the exclusive 3D-sensor supplier for Apple Vision Pro (KED Global, 2024-02-14) while supplying ~70% of iPhone camera modules. Luxshare reportedly stopped Vision Pro production at the start of 2025 (IDC via FT). Camera-module and assembly chain. Within this file only Luxshare Precision (Xreal shareholder) and Goertek (XR reference designs at CES 2026) surface, with no documented module supply relationship to any of the six OEMs; Q Tech, CML, Optotune and Sunny have no public link either. Camera-module makers sit between poLight and the OEM ('it is the OEM… who is kind of the big boss'). SHARP mentioned poLight at a Tech-Day and is in dialogue with poLight; Tongxing hosts poLight's final-test capacity. Sunny Optical claims the global No.1 share in smart-glasses imaging modules (1H25 XR revenue RMB 1.2bn) and showed its own AI glasses at CES 2026. It is a module-level competitor/customer for any actuator supplier, with no stated actuator technology. poLight's manufacturing chain: STMicroelectronics has made the PZT thin-film actuator wafers at its 200 mm Agrate fab since the 2014 TFP launch, and Tong Hsing (THEIL) assembled TLenses from at least 2017 (400→1,000 wafers/month plan). ST is also Metalenz's metasurface foundry; no ST-Meta tunable-lens link was found. Camera-module and assembly chain around glasses: Goertek (Meta Quest/Ray-Ban/Ray-Ban Display assembler), Luxshare (Vision Pro assembly, possible Meta glasses share), Sunny Optical (smart-glasses ramp, AF cameras for AR), Cowell/Largan (Vision Pro modules) and STMicro (poLight's piezo-MEMS foundry). No teardown identifies a camera-module maker or AF actuator in any Meta glasses.

Cadence: 58 day/month-dated non-press signals; median gap 27 days overall, 8 days since 2025; longest silence 2000 days.

**2014-09-23 → 2021-06-30: ST and Tong Hsing backbone**  
ST unveiled its thin-film piezo process on 2014-09-23 with poLight as 'one of the first customers' and Agrate 200 mm volume for mid-2015; by Q1 2017 ST made the actuator and Tong Hsing assembled, with a 400 to 1,000 wafers/month plan and wafers buffered for 1H 2018 delivery. The 2020 assembly line slipped to Q4 2020 'due to resource constraints' while ST wafer deliveries ran Q4 2020-Q2 2021 and production moved toward a lower-cost factory (the Philippines); that buffered inventory is why no new wafers were needed in 2025-2026.

**2020-03-01 → 2025-10-30: The module-maker TLens trail**  
O-Film's product page has carried a 'T-Lens' miniaturised AF module since March 2020 (smaller X/Y, faster, ultra-low power, no magnetic interference); Sunny Opotech filed CN115877539A on 2021-09-29 for a 'liquid lens (T-lens)' integrated inside an AF/OIS motor; a 2022 forum thread called TLens 'the focus of many CM vendors (Sunny, QTech, O-Film)'. A forum-posted LinkedIn excerpt has a Foxconn camera-module engineer completing 'TLens fast-focus camera module driver development' in Jan-Jun 2024 in a role serving Microsoft, Amazon and Varjo; Primax's HOC module for AR/VR glasses (2024-08-29) names no actuator; Shenzhen United Imaging's 12 MP module for AI glasses (2025-04-11) is fixed focus; Luxshare's CIOE 2025 glasses used a Sony IMX681 with EIS and no AF; and Chongqing TS-Precision markets a 'TLens Camera Module' for smart glasses, which poLight's CEO described on 2025-10-30 as an off-the-shelf camera. 'T-Lens' is used generically by some of these makers, so a module brand name alone does not prove poLight's part.

**2021-06-01 → 2025-12-17: Meta and Apple assembly chains**  
ST-Metalenz metasurface optics went from partnership (2021-06) to a 300 mm fab licence with >140M units shipped (2025-07-10). Luxshare was the sole Vision Pro contract manufacturer (2023-07-03), LG Innotek its exclusive 3D-sensor supplier (2024-02-14) and Cowell its external-camera supplier with Apple at 98.1% of revenue (Guojin, 2025-10-30); LG Innotek had also pushed to supply camera modules for Google's AR glasses (2022-04-07) and took a stake in AOE Optronics for XR lenses (2024-01-18). Goertek is the core or exclusive ODM for Meta, Sony and Pico with ~80% of high-end VR/AR assembly (财联社, 2023-11-18), joined the Ray-Ban/Oakley Meta chain in 2025 (OFweek, 2025-08-09) and built Hypernova (2025-09-16); Sunny supplied Quest Pro camera lenses and modules (Zhihu teardown), is 'global No.1' in smart-glasses imaging modules (FY2024, H1 2025) and is reported, with hedges, as the Ray-Ban Meta 12 MP module maker (2025-09-10); on 2025-12-17 Sunny took 33.33% of Goertek Optics for ~RMB 1.9bn. Actuator technology is unstated throughout.

**2021-09-09 → 2027-12-31: ODM and lens-maker TLens filings**  
Full-text checks show lens, module and ODM makers designing around a voltage-driven TLens-type element, none naming poLight, and the construction differs. Goertek's, Q Tech's and Jiangxi Shengtai's texts (Shengtai's AF module granted 2024-12-27) describe poLight's construction, a piezo film deforming a membrane over polymer; Sunny's describe liquid-filled elements: Sunny Opotech's T-lens in a motor (2021-09-29), Zhejiang Sunny's 'bendable film, liquid material and filter' T-LENS (2024-03-14) and its AR/VR front-camera 'Tlens module' (filed 2026-03-04). Sunny Opotech's internal-focusing grant (priority 2021-09-09, granted 2026-01-30) rejects TLENS for field curvature. Huaqin's VR see-through lens (granted 2025-04-08; F/2.1, 120 degrees, 20 cm-5 m) glosses its adjustable element as a 'T lens' once; Kinko cites TLens only in background. Goertek XR filed four applications in 91 days (2024-06-03, 2024-09-02) with TLens or T-Lens in dependent claims, one for gaze-driven VST focus; all are in examination. No filing names a product, customer or supplier.

**2022-02-01 → 2026-10-04: Philippine line, Q Tech line and the missing customs trail**  
poLight's own filings give the physical chain: wafers from ST's 8-inch fab in Italy, assembly and test at Tong Hsing in the Philippines (all of it since Q3 2023) and a Q Tech line in China. Capacity promises ran far ahead of shipments: 1.5M a month by mid-2022, against about 200k assembly and 400-500k test installed in October 2025, a doubling planned by end-2026, and no new MEMS wafers ordered in 2024, 2025 or H1 2026 (inventory 'several millions'). Tong Hsing approved a PHP 668m capital increase (2026-09-10) that does not mention TLens. No customs or trade-statistics source shows a TLens shipment, but the sweep could not have found one: Meta's visible US manifests stop on 2025-06-09 and show accessories, the ImportYeti search could not be read, and a million lenses is about US$2m, below the noise of every aggregate series.

**2026-01-05 → 2027-12-31: 2026 ramp signals and the CIOE sighting**  
Luxshare announced a US$520m, 9m-unit/yr Vietnam VR line tied to Meta (2026-01-05); ChinaTalk mapped Goertek assembly and Sunny camera modules for Ray-Ban Meta and Display (2026-01-07); Goertek's CES 2026 reference designs used an electrically tunable liquid-crystal lens for displays, not camera AF. Sunny's FY2025 XR revenue rose 20.8% to ~RMB 8.58bn with AR camera-module revenue up ~800% (DBS, 2026-04-01), though 2026 'may remain soft' on overseas launch timing; Seeya put the Phoenix OLEDoS panel into mass production in May 2026 (>1m by late August); TechInsights found a Sony 12 MP sensor and no actuator in the Display (2026-06-10). Sunny's H1-2026 results (2026-08-26/27) said smart glasses 'have entered the volume ramp-up phase', listed 'compact high-resolution AF' for AR glasses and called 'large-scale AR product orders from top clients' for next year still in verification; DBS (2026-08-28) made the FY27 smart-glasses ramp its catalyst and Citi (2026-09-24) named Goertek and Sunny VR Glasses beneficiaries. At CIOE (2026-09-09/11) Luxshare listed a 'T-LENS Camera' among its AR optical products beside its Lark glasses; Sunny showed no AF module but advertised for a variable-focus lens engineer. The 2026-09-20 supplier lists give Phoenix Qualcomm, Goertek assembly and pancake, and a Seeya panel; the Sony sensors and Sunny modules sit in the AI-glasses paragraph, so no camera-module or actuator vendor is named for Phoenix.

### Meta patents & people (supplier; 83 dated signals)

Meta-side patents, papers, job posts and people evidence relevant to autofocus. Includes the 2025 Reality Labs paper arguing against autofocus in all-day AI glasses (a counter-signal), a job post for passthrough camera IQ, piezo tunable-lens AF patents reportedly citing poLight, and a LinkedIn claim of a piezo tunable-lens AF module qualified for AR/VR/MR. Meta patent filings on wearable cameras with low-power autofocus (US20230280637A1, abandoned May 2025; US12493197B2, granted Dec 2025) cite CML and poLight prior art. These are examiner citations, not supply evidence, but show Meta engineering actuator-level AF for wearables. Meta holds a cluster of wearable-camera patents describing a PZT thin-film piezo tunable lens for >100° FOV cameras and a tunable-lens barrel for AR glasses. US 12,663,619 B2 (granted 2026-06-23) cites three poLight TLens documents retrieved 2022-10-19, and ex-Meta inventor Lidu Huang says he led a piezo tunable-lens AF module through AR/VR/MR reliability qualification; no Meta fab or Meta-ST deal was found. Meta Platforms Technologies' patent and people trail: a 2022–2023 cluster of piezo-membrane tunable-lens camera filings (window / polymer / glass membrane / thin-film PZT) granted Dec 2025 – Jun 2026, with US 12,663,619's IDS listing three poLight TLens documents retrieved Oct 2022. Inventor Lidu Huang's LinkedIn says the piezo AF module passed full AR/VR/MR reliability qualification before he left in Apr 2025. This is the strongest circumstantial evidence that Meta's autofocus glasses camera is TLens-adjacent. Meta's patent and people evidence: the granted wide-FOV PZT tunable-autofocus patent US 12,663,619 (citing three 2022 poLight documents), lens-barrel tunable-lens patents and the Sept 2026 continuation, plus filings citing CML and poLight, and a former engineer's LinkedIn claim of a qualified piezoelectric tunable-lens AF module. Shows R&D direction, not the production BOM.

Cadence: 80 day/month-dated non-press signals; median gap 20 days overall, 11 days since 2025; longest silence 3562 days.

**2017-12-01 → 2023-08-28: Lidu Huang era filings**  
Huang moved from Western Digital to Apple as a camera-system researcher in Dec 2017 (named on Apple's US 10,881,028) and joined Meta Reality Labs as 'Camera Actuator Architect' in 2020, 'working on miniature AF/OIS cameras optimized for AR/VR devices'. His first Meta filing was a metamaterial projector (2021-10-28) and a VCM-based power-saving AF camera (2022-04-12) marks the pre-piezo phase; then came the dense tunable-lens run: wristband AF citing poLight (2022-01-04), a wearable camera citing four CML documents (2022-05-31), macro low-power AF (2022-07-12), a 'flat-surfaced tunable optical lens' with PZT film for smart-glasses cameras (2022-07-22), the lens-barrel provisional (2022-07-26), retrieval of poLight's TLens Add-In pages (2022-10-19), an FPCB-mounted tunable lens (2022-11-08), the wide-FOV 107-degree, F/2.2, TTL 5.0 mm assembly (2023-02-08), the omnibus with '~6 mW, ~2 ms, no moving parts' (2023-03-02), the gaze-driven AF passthrough camera (2023-03-31) and closed-loop capacitance sensing (2023-08-28). Seven piezo-relevant priorities in 20 months describe a TLens-like stack; later piezo-lens priorities (driver IC 2023-11-15, exposed camera 2025-02-12) continue the run, none naming a supplier.

**2020-09-01 → 2026-10-08: What the public LinkedIn and job-post trail verifies**  
Very little: none of the LinkedIn items is independently verified. Profiles are login-gated; the researcher read search snippets that two checkers could not open or re-find (HTTP 999). Lidu Huang's snippet (Meta, to April 2025) claims a 'miniature piezoelectric tunable lens AF camera module' that passed AR/VR/MR qualification with 'high NTI yields'; he is a named inventor on Meta's own lens filings and left about three months before Program A's first order, so the text names no supplier and fits an in-house lens as well as a bought one. A module lead's 'NTI dToF/ Tlens' bullet shows no employer or dates (Meta is one of nine listed employers); a Hon Hai manager's TLens bullet lists Amazon, Google and Microsoft as customers. The 'led the autofocus work' post and 'DRI for TLens' line are forum paraphrases no index returns.

**2023-09-13 → 2025-12-12: Alternatives, qualification and productization**  
Meta also filed MEMS Alvarez lenses over SPAD pixels for eye tracking (2023-09-13, granted 2026-05-12) and, nine months after the gaze-driven AF priority, a moving-single-element MEMS autofocus for pass-through MR (priority 2023-12-06, published 2025-06-12, pending) citing LG Innotek, Samsung and Nidec. An in-field actuator calibration application (priority 2024-09-17) names a 'piezoelectric (PZT) actuated tunable lens' among the VCM, SMA and MEMS actuators recalibrated after drops and drift, and a camera module with a tunable lens and wafer-level optics (priority 2024-12-19, filed 2025-11-14) allows 'polymer' or 'liquid' tunable-lens technology. Jason Hartlove opened SPIE 2025 for Meta; the CML-citing wearable camera was allowed 2025-01-21 and abandoned 2025-05-08. Huang left in April 2025 with a profile saying a piezo tunable-lens module passed 'full reliability qualifications for AR/VR/MR'; Reality Labs' 2025-04-17 paper argued against autofocus in all-day glasses; a closed Seoul optical-systems posting gave 'AF camera actuator (e.g. VCM)' as a preferred skill; the wide-FOV application took a final rejection on 2025-07-10. Productization-type filings followed: camera hazard protection with 20 inventors including Huang (2025-08-22), the non-provisional calibration filing (2025-09-17), the US 12,493,197 macro-AF grant (2025-12-09) and unibody camera anchoring into the frame (2025-12-12).

**2023-11-15 → 2026-08-13: In Meta's own words: no 'TLens'**  
Full-text reading of Meta's own filings in round 3: the +/-50 V piezo-actuator driver IC (priority 2023-11-15, WO2025117178A1 published 2025-06-05, 278k characters) speaks only of a 'piezoelectrically-driven tunable lens' and a 'tunable lens driver integrated circuit'; 'Exposed camera architectures' (priority 2025-02-12, published 2026-08-13; Huang, Chen, Li) claims an exposed front group and a deformable-surface tunable lens, uses a sleeve to route shock past it, and describes a 0 to +/-5 D piezo membrane for 'AR glasses, smartglasses, or a VR headset'. Neither text, nor the camera-module and barrel-via applications or a thermal filing whose 'Tlens' is a chart label, names TLens or poLight; poLight appears only as cited prior art. Cadence: the driver IC came 11 weeks after the closed-loop priority (2023-08-28), the exposed camera 15 months later; publication trails priority by 18-19 months. The texts fit a bought TLens-class part or an own membrane lens and name no supplier, product or date.

**2026-02-05 → 2027-12-31: Grants, hires and job posts before launch**  
Huang's exposed-camera filing was lodged 2026-02-05; US 12,547,244 (gaze-driven AF passthrough) was granted 2026-02-10; the wide-FOV application was allowed 2026-02-23; the calibration application published 2026-03-19; a barrel-via continuation followed (2026-04-30); US 12,631,847 (lens barrel with an integrated tunable lens) was granted 2026-05-19 and US 12,663,619 (citing three poLight documents) 2026-06-23; US 2026/0177877 and 0177835 published 2026-06-25 and the barrel-via continuation publication six days before Connect (2026-09-17). Patrick Llull joined from Apple as sensor-to-display architect (May 2026), and a Reality Labs engineer's LinkedIn post, seen as a forum screenshot of an auto-translation, is paraphrased as saying he led the VR Glasses autofocus work over years. Job posts cluster around Connect: Opto-Mechanical Engineer, Camera (Active Alignment, ramp, 2026-09-22), Camera and Depth Electrical Engineer ('auto-focus electrical design', about 2026-09-16 to 22), a next-generation smart-glasses sensor lead (about 2026-09-30), camera-systems software and sensor research roles (2026-10-05), and a camera-IQ lead and an undated camera-system role live on 2026-10-06. Meta's careers site (via mirrors) and six job boards show no tunable-lens, piezo, MEMS-actuator or TLens wording. A forum-posted, undated excerpt of a former Meta DFx engineer ('DRI for TLens camera process development, drove 2 Eng mini-builds') is the closest Meta-TLens link; a second excerpt's employer is cropped, so it may be a supplier. First actions on the 2025-11-14 filings are projections.

### Analysts, brokers & press (supplier; 52 dated signals)

Market-sizing and shipment claims from Omdia, which puts Meta at 7.4m AI glasses in 2025 and 3.4m (81% share) in 1H26. These volumes set the scale of any Meta design-win for an autofocus supplier, even though the mainstream glasses remain fixed-focus. Only Analyst Group (commissioned, NOK 9.0/share) formally covers poLight. DBS covers Q Tech and cites 'low-power tunable lenses' as a smart-glasses opportunity but, in the accessible notes, never names poLight, Meta or 2027; the alleged DBS 'H1 2027' Meta/Q Tech/poLight claim remains unverified. Press and analyst commentary relevant to the SMA-vs-TLens comparison: Karl Guttag's CES 2023 power figures (CML ~64 mW moving vs TLens <6 mW), Yole's read of the Alps licence, and Everbright's sizing of the TDK→Q Tech deal. Analyst material in this file is limited to Patsnap's 2026-09-17 liquid-lens AF actuator patent landscape (LG Innotek 7, Corning 5, Meta 3, Apple 3; filings down 67% 2021-2024). Analyst, broker and press claims: DBS's Aug-2026 Q Tech note publicly cites "low-power tunable lenses" in smart glasses, while the Meta/1H27 mass-production sentence attributed to it is gated and unverified; DBS on Sunny flags an FY27 smart-glasses ramp; Counterpoint and Everbright add manufacturing-share and Cowell colour. Press and analyst claims: KGOnTech's March 2023 CES/PW report placed TLens in the Magic Leap 2 and Sharp's CES-2023 VR prototype at <6 mW, an early confirmed-in-product data point for poLight in head-worn devices. Analyst, broker, market-data and in-thread assistant claims: DBS Research (26 Aug 2026) is the only source naming a Meta + Q Tech + poLight project with 1H27 mass production; Omdia, Counterpoint and TrendForce supply market sizing; the GPT-6 Pro assistant's probability estimates, rankings and valuation models are logged here.

**2022-03-10 → 2025-06-19: Technology comparisons and the first Meta guesses**  
Pareto's 2022-03-10 TV interview is its only public poLight item (Pareto hosts the 2026-10-30 CMD). Karl Guttag's CES 2023 notes set CML's 8-wire SMA (~3.2 V/20 mA) against TLens's '<6 mW' (2023-03-04); Yole inferred a CML licence behind Alps's SMA production (2023-04-14); the VR market was 6.9m units in 2024 with Meta at ~77%. CMBI expected Sunny to be 'a major camera supplier for new AI glasses from leading brands, such as Meta, Xiaomi and Samsung' (2025-02-13); 开源 (2025-03-10) and 国盛 (2025-03-19, 'supplier qualifications at several international top brands') covered Q Tech's XR progress; 潮电智库 wrote on 2025-04-30 that poLight's top US customer is 'very likely Meta' and that Q Tech may integrate poLight lenses into camera or pancake modules; Everbright sized the TDK deal at 2,000+ patents and 2,000+ employees and called micro actuators 'decisive' for AF (2025-05-13); VRAR星球 cited an undated DNB Markets note on Meta or Apple adopting TLens-like solutions (2025-06-19). Nobody yet connected these actuators to a dated glasses launch.

**2025-07-11 → 2026-10-08: DBS trail: four notes, one Meta sentence**  
DBS wrote on Q Tech on 2025-07-11, 2025-08-12, 2026-03-17 and 2026-08-26, with none since (43 days). The first says piezo tunable lenses 'co-developed with poLight' are in customer sampling for AI glasses and service robots; the second and third place poLight in an XR optics stack, naming no OEM. Only the 2026-08-26 note names Meta: a Meta project combining Q Tech modules with poLight's low-power tunable lens 'is expected to enter mass production in 1H27', and 'products are already being shipped to Meta and Samsung' beside optical engines. The PDF is verified verbatim (page 4 per the research file, not re-checked), but the sentence is unsourced sell-side inference about 'a Meta project', not specifically the VR Glasses, and DBS's own Meta note (2026-05-08) has no poLight, Q Tech or autofocus term. It came four weeks before Connect.

**2025-10-30 → 2026-08-06: Sell-side turns to glasses**  
Guojin put Cowell in Vision Pro's camera chain and 'possibly' Apple's AI glasses (2025-10-30/11-03); CTEE reported Phoenix pushed from 2H 2026 to 1H 2027 (2025-12-07, after Business Insider's 12-05 memo story); a 东方财富 column on poLight-Q Tech dwelt on LiDAR and named no XR customer (2026-01-15), the same day a Finansavisen forum thread began speculating about Meta/Apple with an unverified 'DNB says volume orders in 8-16 months' claim; 国元 repeated the TLens/piezo rationale (2026-02-04); a commissioned Analyst Group initiation valued poLight at NOK 9.0 (2026-02-06); Omdia counted 7.4m Meta AI glasses in 2025 (2026-03-05); DBS put Sunny's AR camera-module revenue up ~800% with 2026 soft on overseas launch timing (2026-04-01) and its 2026-05-08 Meta note never mentioned poLight; DeviceBriefing's grant roundup (2026-05-15), TechInsights' Display teardown with no actuator stated (2026-06-10), DBS's Lens Technology initiation with zero poLight/Q Tech/Meta hits (2026-06-16) and UBS on Sunny's 50m-glasses, waveguide-to-ODM ambition (2026-07-05) followed. Analyst Group's Q2 comment (2026-08-06) noted ~NOK 1.8m of Q Tech line support, named no Meta and no 2027, and stated the rule that 'a design-win is classified once the product is confirmed for market release, typically around a product announcement'.

**2026-08-24 → 2027-09-30: DBS names Meta; Connect commentary; the teardown clock**  
Everbright's 1H26 Q Tech note mentioned XR only as a second curve (2026-08-24). DBS's Q Tech note of 2026-08-26 (BUY, target cut to HKD 12.60 from 15.0) cites 'low-power tunable lenses', says Q Tech's AR optical engines are 'already being shipped to Meta and Samsung' and states on p.4 that a Meta project combining Q Tech modules with poLight's tunable lens 'is expected to enter mass production in 1H27': located in the PDF, but unsourced sell-side inference, and DBS's 2026-05-08 Meta note never mentions poLight. TDN Direkt reported the poLight insider sale the next day; DBS's Sunny note (2026-08-28) made the FY27 smart-glasses ramp its catalyst. September brought leaked Phoenix renders (2026-09-12), Digitimes' >80% Chinese supplier share (2026-09-17), Patsnap's liquid-lens landscape (LG Innotek 7, Corning 5, Meta 3, Apple 3), the AR圈 supplier list with no camera-module vendor (2026-09-20), Omdia's 3.4m Meta glasses in 1H26 (2026-09-22), Connect hands-ons with the focus mechanism undescribed (2026-09-23), Morgan Stanley's 'VR glasses a 2027 growth driver' and Citi's 'Goertek and Sunny beneficiaries, volume likely limited' (2026-09-24), and AI-assistant estimates (2026-09-25) that are model output, not evidence. No public Pareto, Arctic, SB1, Redeye or DNB Carnegie note was found, but Norwegian research is paywalled. First VR Glasses teardowns are expected Apr-Sep 2027 (Display precedent: shipped 2025-09-30, iFixit 2025-10-08, TechInsights 2026-06-10).

**2026-09-02 → 2026-10-08: Sizing after Connect: IDC and the panel count**  
Sizing remains thin. IDC (2026-09-16) forecasts XR headset and glasses shipments up 26.3% in 2026 and 40.5% in 2027; its Connect recap (2026-09-25) says passthrough VR peaked in 2024, then fell 44% in 2025 and a further 27% this year, calls the US$1,299 VR Glasses 'priced like a PC' for enthusiasts and enterprise pilots, and gives no unit forecast. The Elec (2026-08-28, repeated by Digitimes on 2026-09-02, paywalled) reported that Seeya has made Phoenix panels since May, about 1 million by late August at two per headset, and that Meta may adjust production to market response after launch. No public TrendForce, Counterpoint or Wellsenn figure for the VR Glasses turned up, so Meta's volume plan is unknown, and nothing in these notes mentions actuators or poLight. The Q3 report on 2026-10-29 is the first cheap public test of whether lens volumes are flowing.

## 6. What the earlier ChatGPT research thread established

The thread tests one thesis: that poLight's TLens piezo-MEMS tunable lens is the autofocus element in the stereo passthrough cameras of Meta's ~100 g 'Meta VR Glasses', announced at Connect on 23 September 2026 for a spring-2027 launch at USD 1,299.99. Meta's developer specifications confirm 'color stereoscopic (26 PPD) passthrough with autofocus and depth sensing' but name no actuator or supplier, so the question is purely supplier identity.

Strongest evidence for poLight: Meta's granted patent US 12,663,619 (granted 23 June 2026) claims a flexible membrane, hard substrate, deformable polymer and thin-film PZT actuators - essentially TLens's architecture - and cites three 2022 poLight documents; a documented chain in which an anonymous top-tier U.S. OEM that had qualified TLens for years backed Q Technology's ~NOK 171m investment and dedicated TLens line (April 2025), followed by qualification POs (Aug 2025, Feb 2026, Jun 2026) for 'very advanced, high-end glasses' that could 'ramp in huge volumes'; Q Tech's 2024 'US M brand' XR vendor code; DBS Research (26 Aug 2026) stating a Meta project combining Q Tech modules with poLight's tunable lens enters mass production in 1H27; and a former Meta engineer's LinkedIn profile citing a 'miniature piezoelectric tunable lens AF camera module' that passed AR/VR/MR reliability qualification.

Strongest counter-evidence: poLight has never named Meta; its CEO confirmed on 19 Aug 2026 that the three headline programs are different end customers, so clues cannot be stacked; the 2026 design-in targets a 2026 product; the Q Tech program is still 'qualification' with only ~NOK 2.5m of attributable orders; DBS gives no source and disclaims verification; Meta's patents could describe an in-house or third-party PZT lens; CML, Optotune and VCM makers cannot be excluded.

Final probability: estimates oscillated 30-50% -> 62% -> 68% -> 78% -> 65% -> 88% -> 85% before settling at ~70% (60-65% without DBS) that TLens is in the spring-2027 Meta VR Glasses, with ~90% that Meta is the Q Tech-backed OEM. Not covered: teardowns or any direct Meta/poLight/Q Tech confirmation, full USPTO file wrappers, CML's latest accounts, Q Tech primary filings linking the 2024 M-brand customer to the 2025 investment, poLight's cumulative 2026 order total, actual Meta volumes or camera power figures, and the LinkedIn individual's identity.

Open questions the thread left (carried into this research):

- Which autofocus technology and supplier did Meta select for the spring-2027 VR Glasses' stereo passthrough cameras? Meta's specs confirm autofocus and depth sensing but name neither actuator nor supplier; no teardown, supplier disclosure or poLight design-win/mass-production announcement tied to a U.S. top-tier OEM has appeared.
- Which, if any, of poLight's three separate consumer programs is Meta: A (Q Tech-backed top-tier U.S. OEM qualification), B (Oct-2025 ~NOK 5m AR head-worn camera project), or C (2026 consumer AR/MR design-in whose product is expected in 2026)? Could the Q Tech-backed OEM be Meta but for a different generation/model?
- Is the Q Tech-backed top-tier U.S. OEM Meta, Apple, Google, Snap, Amazon or another company? poLight has never named Meta.
- Who is the customer behind the Oct-2025 NOK 5m AR camera project, did the modules shipped end-Q2 2026 pass validation, and is it a platform/ecosystem company (e.g. Android XR/Google)? Isaksen declined to explain the ecosystem arrangement.
- Who is the 2026 consumer AR/MR design-in customer whose product launches in 2026, and was that product delayed?
- Is Q Tech's 2024 'US M brand' XR vendor-code customer the same top-tier U.S. OEM that backed the 2025 Q Tech-poLight investment? No primary-source sentence found saying yes; can a Q Tech report, transcript or Q&A be found that links them?
- Is Q Technology a camera-module supplier to Meta's Reality Labs/Quest hardware (even historically), and is it the passthrough-camera module supplier for the 2027 VR Glasses?
- Does the DBS-described Meta + Q Tech + poLight H1 2027 mass-production project correspond specifically to the spring-2027 Meta VR Glasses or to a different Meta glasses product, and what is DBS's underlying source?
- When will the Q Tech-backed OEM's production ramp begin, what volumes does it need (Q Tech's initial line is not sized for eventual volume), and has product-level (camera/headset) qualification been completed as distinct from component-level qualification of Q Tech-made lenses?
- Will the next Q Tech/top-tier OEM order jump from NOK 0.7-1m qualification batches to several million NOK (assistant expects a first production PO of ~NOK 5-15m by late Q4 2026 / Q1 2027) with wording shifting from 'qualification' to 'production/ramp'? Has poLight upgraded the Q Tech case to design-in or mass production?
- What is the cumulative 2026 order flow from the Q Tech-backed OEM, and which (if any) TWedge POs belong to that OEM and would raise the attributable total above NOK 2.5m?
- Does Meta's granted patent US 12,663,619 (citing 2022 poLight documents) reflect in-house development, licensing of poLight technology, or a supply relationship? Who introduced the poLight references (applicant, examiner or search), did poLight's prior art cause the narrowing amendments, and would use of the underlying technology require a poLight license?
- Does Meta's production passthrough camera actually use the PZT/polymer/membrane construction claimed in US12663619 (constant FOV during focusing), or a VCM/SMA/MEMS architecture from Meta's other filings? The patent-to-production link is missing.
- Do the Meta patent specifications (5.0 mm TTL, ~20 cm minimum focus, <1 mm BFL) differ from poLight's public 6.8 mm TTL / 10 cm reference design because of a different design, a customized/in-house tunable element, or a further-developed poLight part?
- Is the 'via' electrical feed-through in US20260276939A1 a Meta-specific novelty compatible with a bare poLight TLens, or does it indicate a different (in-house or third-party) PZT-polymer lens supplier?
- Who supplied the piezoelectric tunable lens in the Meta 'miniature piezoelectric tunable lens AF camera module' described on the LinkedIn profile (poLight/TLens vs another piezo supplier)? Was that module selected for the spring-2027 glasses, or did Meta evaluate alternatives in parallel? What does the full profile say and who is the individual?
- Are the LinkedIn module's reliability tests and poLight's still-ongoing Q Tech qualification (Feb 2026) different levels/revisions or different projects?
- Does anything publicly exclude CML as the autofocus supplier for Meta's 2027 glasses? Are CML's 2021 'US technology giants' engagements and 2023 XR commercial projects the same customers, still ongoing, and about camera AF or display optics? Does CML's latest financial accounts PDF (not retrieved) contain relevant contract disclosures?
- Could CML supply a different function in the glasses (display-optics focus, OIS) even if not the piezo AF? Would CML's Zero Hold Power actually beat TLens on energy in continuous stereo-passthrough AF, and are there measurements of whether a current CML SMA actuator meets Meta's speed/power requirements?

Is there any product-specific comparison showing Optotune or a VCM competing for Meta's actual stereo-passthrough camera?

## 9. Coverage, gaps and method

Signals by source type: company 493, press 241, patent_office 129, exchange 98, other 86, analyst 51, forum 27.

Method: round 1 — nine research agents compiled dated timelines per producer and supplier from company newsrooms, Oslo Børs / HKEX / SEC filings, Google Patents, developer documentation and reputable press, with forum and unnamed-source items marked as rumour; a digest of the earlier ChatGPT thread supplied the starting hypotheses; the rows were converted to a common schema, deduplicated per lane, cross-matched against launch windows, criticised for completeness, and the load-bearing dates were re-checked against their cited sources. Round 2 — five agents on Meta's autofocus program, the Chinese supply chain and analyst trail, module makers, poLight's historical lead times and the primary documents; 128 load-bearing rows checked by two independent fact-checkers each. Round 3 — a full-text patent sweep for TLens / poLight (2024-2026); all 69 rows and windows checked on the registers by two independent checkers each, false positives dropped, and the synthesis audited by eighteen skeptics (evidence, logic, dates-and-arithmetic) before an editor of record rewrote findings, matches and the estimate.

NEXT RESEARCH TASKS
First, build the module-maker evidence the dataset lacks. Read Goertek, Sunny, Luxshare and Foxconn filings, plus the Citi and DBS supply-chain notes, and obtain the Quest 3/3S teardown. This tests the strongest rival to the Q Tech chain, which is who assembles the VR Glasses camera. It would also show whether Meta's current headset cameras are fixed-focus, VCM or tunable, and it brings the thin modules and analysts lanes up to the level of the poLight and Meta lanes. Second, break the single-source dependence on DBS. Re-check page 4 of the 2026-08-26 PDF, then look for an independent second source, such as sell-side notes from other brokers on Q Tech, Q Tech's Q&A at its interim results, an investor meeting transcript, or poLight's own wording around the 2026-10-29 and 10-30 events. Combine this with the CNIPA and Meta patent-citation work and the Q Tech connected-party circular, to test whether the Meta and Q Tech pairing is real or one analyst's inference. Third, set up monitoring and pre-registration for the dated tests. Run daily Newsweb and HKEX watchers, archive Meta's product, developer and careers pages weekly, and prepare a template for FCC grant (2AGOZ) and teardown capture. Each new item can then be scored at once against the pre-stated thresholds: 0.62 on a design-in, 0.30 on none by 2027-02-24, and near zero or near one on a teardown.
